C0500.d: C0500 flags lost continuity in the left front wheel speed sensor circuit. An active sensor draws a steady current even with the car parked; Allegro gives 7 and 14 mA as the usual levels of a two-wire interface, so a reading near zero means a broken path.
s: ABS, ESC and traction control warning lamps on, check-engine lamp on some makes
ABS, stability control and hill start assist unavailable
Scan tool shows no left front wheel speed while driving
c: Sensor plug corroded or loose, or a wire broken along the wheel arch
ABS module supply, fuse or fusible link faulty (Mitsubishi lists these)

C0501.d: C0501 means the left front speed signal is present but does not fit the situation. GM shows how differently this is judged: its 2016 hybrid tables flag the code when that wheel reads 0 mph while the other three exceed 7.45 mph at a vehicle speed above 11.8 mph (Type A), whereas the 2023 tables test the air gap and set it when magnetic flux stays below 2.2 mT for at least five wheel turns, as Type B with two trips.
s: ABS and stability warning lamps on after driving, not at key-on
Unexpected ABS or traction control intervention at low speed
Code stored in the engine controller without MIL (Stellantis)
c: Sensor not fully seated or air gap to the tone ring too large
Tire on the left front differs in size from the specified one
Tone ring or magnetic encoder damaged or dirty
Control module software sets the code falsely (Stellantis reflash)

C0502.d: C0502 reports the left front sensor circuit below its valid level, mostly a grounded wire or a supply that has sagged. In GM's 2019 tables (19OBDG03D) the brake module's Polaris ASIC sets C0502 for three conditions: the low side shorted to ground, tested only at power-up or after clearing codes (100 ms); sensor undervoltage (20 ms); and, unusually, an open sensor drawing under 3.5 mA, which other GM tables file as C0
s: ABS and ESC lamps on right after starting
Parking brake warning or electric parking brake functions restricted on some models
c: Sensor wire chafed through to ground or poorly crimped in the connector
Sensor supply voltage too low (battery, fuse or module output)
Internal short in the left front sensor

C0503.d: With C0503 the left front circuit reads above its permitted level, which in practice means the signal wire is in contact with battery voltage. GM's 2016 hybrid tables set it when the signal line exceeds 12 V for 0.12 s; the 2023 tables look at current instead and react above 50 mA, many times what a healthy active sensor draws.
s: ABS and ESC warnings directly after switching on
Check-engine lamp on some makes (GM Type A, Mitsubishi)
Brake assist and hill descent control switched off
c: Signal wire shorted to a battery-voltage feed
Internal short in the left front sensor
Sensor input stage in the ABS module defective

C0504.d: C0504 points to a left front speed signal that jumps or produces far too many edges, not one that is missing. GM's 2016 hybrid brake module stores a time stamp for every sensor edge in a buffer and sets C0504 within 0.03 s when that buffer overflows; the 2023 tables apply the same idea to a DMA transfer unit receiving time stamps too often.
s: ABS lamp and service stability message on the driver display
Fault comes and goes with road surface or steering angle
c: Metal debris or dirt on the reluctor ring (GM PIT5707)
Loose contact in the sensor plug or a wire breaking under movement

C0505.d: C0505 says the left front wheel speed is out of step with the other wheels although the circuit tests pass. GM's 2019 tables (19OBDG03D) group several comparisons under this code: a missing sensor, meaning this wheel shows under 1.5 km/h while another exceeds 6 km/h (3 to 120 s depending on speed); a dropout check paused after sudden accelerations; a start-up check that runs until 15 km/h; and the reverse case, where
s: ABS/ESC lamps after a drive, often following a tire change
Traction control intervenes although wheels are not slipping
c: Tire of a different size or heavily worn tire on the left front
Sensor not seated correctly, air gap out of tolerance
Demagnetized or damaged magnetic encoder ring

C0506.d: C0506 reports an open or grounded circuit at the right front wheel speed sensor. GM's 2023 tables describe it as a grounded or interrupted line, recognized from the signal-line current: below 3.8 mA for 0.12 s, Type A, and only evaluated after the start-up sensor test has finished without a supply undervoltage.
s: ABS, ESC and traction control lamps on from start-up
Right front wheel speed reads zero in live data
c: Broken wire or open contact between ABS module and right front sensor
Old stored code after repair, vehicle not yet driven

C0507.d: C0507 flags an implausible right front speed signal. In GM's 2019 tables the brake module's ASIC watches the sensor current itself: a level hanging in the grey zones between 7 and 14 mA or 14 and 28 mA for 750 ms points to a high-resistance harness or leakage to battery voltage.
s: ABS/ESC lamps after driving off
Code present only in the engine controller during a full vehicle scan
c: Corroded contacts or damaged insulation causing resistance or leakage current
Damaged tone ring or wrong tire size on the right front
Engine controller software storing the code falsely (Stellantis)

C0508.d: C0508 reports the right front sensor circuit below range. A 2024 Jeep Wrangler case from the Stellantis STAR center shows a typical picture: after an earlier repair the ABS lamp came on with C0508-00, ABS disabled and implausible-speed network codes; the sensor harness had been pinched and only needed rerouting.
s: ABS lamp on, often right after a repair
Additional network codes about implausible wheel or vehicle speed
Parking brake warning on some models
c: Sensor harness pinched or misrouted after suspension or brake work
Poorly crimped terminal in the sensor connector (Audi)

C0509.d: C0509 means the right front sensor line carries more current or voltage than allowed. GM's 2019 tables (19OBDG03D) set it within 100 ms when the high-side current passes 40 mA, or when the Polaris ASIC reports either sensor line shorted to battery or an overcurrent on the low side; it is Type A.
s: ABS and ESC lamps on immediately, check-engine lamp on some makes
ABS, EBD and hill start assist suspended
c: Sensor line chafed against a battery-voltage wire
Right front sensor drawing excess current due to an internal short
Sensor supply driver in the ABS module defective

C050A.d: C050A is the erratic-signal code for the right front sensor. GM's 2019 tables show how this is judged: an unfiltered wheel acceleration above 491 m/s² feeds a counter that latches the fault at 40 s and decays again on clean readings, so only persistently unrealistic jumps set it; a separate check trips when the edge count exceeds 55 (25 ms).
s: ABS lamp and stability system message that appear and disappear
Pulsing brake pedal or ABS action at low speed without wheel lock
c: Metal debris or heavy dirt on the right front reluctor ring
Missing tone-ring teeth or excessive wheel bearing play
Electromagnetic interference or intermittent contact in the harness

C050B.d: C050B is the correlation code for the right front wheel. GM's 2025 tables (25OBDG04A) rate it Type B, so the MIL waits for a second trip, and add a check not found under C0505 in the 2019 tables: the brake module compares the switching state it requests from the sensor supply driver with the state reported back, an internal module fault rather than a sensor problem.
s: ABS/ESC lamps after the second drive with the fault
Stability and traction control unavailable, normal braking retained
c: Right front tire of a different size or circumference
Sensor-to-ring gap out of tolerance or demagnetized encoder
Internal fault in the ABS module's sensor supply switch (GM)

C050C.d: C050C is stored when the brake controller loses the current path to the left rear speed sensor. GM's 2023 OBD tables (23OBDG07) read 0.12 s at under 3.8 mA in the signal wire as a ground short or a break and rate the code Type A, so the MIL can come on in the first trip.
s: ABS and stability warning lamps on right after key-on, check-engine lamp on some makes
ABS, stability control and on some models electric parking brake functions restricted
Live data shows no left rear wheel speed
c: Sensor lead chafed or torn where it follows the rear suspension
Left rear sensor connector corroded or not latched

C050D.d: C050D says the left rear signal exists but is not trustworthy. In GM's 23OBDG07 tables several checks share this code: a weak magnetic flux under 2.2 mT across at least five wheel turns (detected after 8 s at 3.1 mph or 22 s at 1.24 mph), missing standstill pulses for 3.6 s, and an undervoltage on the sensor supply; all are Type B with two trips, and the tables list Bosch, Continental and DF11i sensor variants.
s: ABS and stability lamps come on only after some driving
Stability or traction control intervenes without reason at low speed
Code may be stored without a lit MIL on some Stellantis models
c: Air gap to the rear encoder too large (sensor not seated, worn or loose hub bearing)
Contact resistance or leakage in the rear sensor wiring
Left rear tire differs in rolling circumference
Control module software sets the code falsely (Stellantis reflash)

C050E.d: C050E reports the left rear sensor circuit pulled below its expected level. GM's 2019 EBCM tables (19OBDG03D) let the Polaris ASIC set it for three separate findings: an open sensor bit, a grounded low side, looked for only at start-up or once codes have been cleared, and sensor undervoltage, which needs only 20 ms; all are Type A with the MIL.
s: ABS, stability and electric parking brake warnings on (Mitsubishi)
ABS and stability control disabled for the rest of the trip
c: Sensor wire grounded against the subframe or body
Moisture or corrosion in the left rear connector
Low supply voltage at the brake module (fuse, battery)

C050F.d: C050F covers the opposite electrical case: the left rear circuit sits too high, as when the signal wire touches a battery-fed conductor. For GM's 2016 hybrids, 12 V surpassed on the signal wire for 0.12 s, with more than 6.9 V system voltage, is the trigger; the 2023 tables instead look at current and flag a signal wire carrying over 50 mA, again within 0.12 s and as Type A.
s: ABS and stability lamps on immediately, MIL on some makes
No ABS regulation, rear brake force distribution in fallback mode
c: Signal wire shorted to a battery-fed circuit in the rear loom
Left rear sensor draws excessive current internally

C0510.d: C0510 flags a left rear speed signal that jumps instead of changing smoothly. GM's 19OBDG03D EBCM logic counts every moment in which the unfiltered wheel acceleration exceeds 491 m/s² at vehicle speeds beyond 3.58 m/s and sets the code once that tally reaches 40 s; a second path latches it within 25 ms when more than 55 edges arrive too quickly.
s: ABS or stability lamp on after bumps, railway crossings or rumble strips
Brief, unexpected ABS pulsing at the rear
Fault often gone after the next ignition cycle
c: Sensor loose in its bore or play in the rear wheel bearing
Missing or damaged teeth, rust flakes on the tone ring
Wire breaking up intermittently as the rear suspension moves
Heavy payload or trailer on rough roads (Ram 3500 case)

C0511.d: C0511 means the left rear speed does not match what the other three wheels report. In GM's 19OBDG03D tables four monitors feed it: missing sensor (this wheel below 1.5 km/h while the rest exceed 6 km/h, 3 to 120 s), dropout (no edges for 150 ms after a valid reading above 30 km/h, with thresholds that depend on axle and brake pedal), fast missing (counted from key-on until 15 km/h is first reached) and too fast (this
s: ABS and stability lamps on after setting off or at moderate speed
Speedometer and driver aids act up after a tire change
c: Left rear tire of a different size or heavily worn compared with the others
Demagnetized encoder or damaged tone ring at the left rear
Wrong sensor fitted after a repair (GM PIT5950)

C0512.d: C0512 is the open-circuit code for the right rear wheel. GM's 2016 hybrid tables run the check only after the sensor self-test has finished and system voltage is above 6.9 V; then 0.12 s with less than 3.8 mA flowing in the signal wire is enough for a Type A entry.
s: ABS and stability lamps on at key-on, sometimes the MIL
Right rear wheel speed reads zero in live data
ABS and traction control unavailable
c: Broken lead or unplugged connector at the right rear
Fuse or power feed of the brake module (Mitsubishi lists it)

C0513.d: C0513 marks a right rear signal that is present but implausible. GM's 2016 hybrid tables catch two patterns: the wheel shows 0 mph while the other three turn and the car exceeds 11.8 mph, and a start-up check in which the right rear stays at zero while the others pass 7.45 mph; both mature at once as Type A, but not during ABS or traction control action.
s: ABS lamp with a service stability message
Lamps come on after driving off, not at key-on
Code stored without MIL on some Stellantis models
c: ABS harness rubbing on the rear drive unit (2024 Silverado EV)
Excessive air gap or damaged encoder at the right rear
Right rear tire of a different size
False setting by control module software (Stellantis)

C0514.d: C0514 reports the right rear sensor circuit below its valid range. GM's 2025 EBCM tables (25OBDG04A) show how broadly that is read: the Polaris ASIC raises an open-sensor bit when the high-side current drops under 3.5 mA, and a separate bit for a low side shorted to ground, both after 100 ms as Type A; the listed suspects run from sensor and harness to the printed circuit board and the ASIC.
s: ABS lamp and service stability message
Electric parking brake warning on some models (Mitsubishi)
ABS and stability control switched off
c: Harness worn through and grounded near the rear axle or drive unit
Brake module circuit board or ASIC faulty (GM lists it)

C0515.d: C0515 says the right rear sensor circuit draws or sees too much. GM's 2025 tables bundle four ASIC flags under this code: high-side current above 40 mA, high side shorted to battery, low-side overcurrent and, perhaps unexpectedly, a low side shorted to ground; each sets it after 100 ms as Type A.
s: ABS and stability lamps on as soon as the self-test ends
Stability and traction control unavailable
c: Insulation damage in the right rear harness causing a short
Sensor supply stage in the brake module defective

C0516.d: C0516 stands for a right rear signal that stutters or spikes. GM's 2025 tables use the 491 m/s² wheel acceleration limit at speeds beyond 3.58 m/s but let the fault mature in about 200 ms of near-continuous violation, sampled every 5 ms, and decay the counter when the signal calms; the 2016 hybrid tables instead set it after a 0.03 s overflow of the timer buffer that stores sensor edges.
s: ABS, stability and traction lamps after rough road sections
Functions return only after the next ignition cycle
c: Rear axle vibration disturbing the signal (GM program 18316)
Damaged tone ring teeth or loosely mounted right rear sensor
Brake module calibration too sensitive, update available

C0517.d: C0517 reports that the right rear speed disagrees with the rest of the vehicle. GM's 2025 tables (25OBDG04A) run missing, dropout, fast-missing and too-fast checks for this wheel; the missing-sensor test, a wheel under 1.5 km/h while others exceed 6 km/h, is rated Type B there, i.e.
s: ABS and stability lamps after driving off or at moderate speed
Code returns after sensor replacement if the true cause is elsewhere
c: Right rear tire not matching the others in size or wear
Weak encoder or excessive air gap at the right rear
Wrong sensor installed during an earlier repair
Sensor supply driver inside the brake module faulty (GM)

C0518.d: C0518 points to a mechanical rather than electrical problem at the left front speed sensor: wrong part, wrong position, a damaged or soiled encoder, or play in the hub. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's tables and Mitsubishi's index file such faults under range or correlation codes instead.
s: ABS and stability lamps on, often recurring after a repair
Uneven or missing left front speed reading at low speed
c: Sensor for the other side fitted or tip turned away from the encoder
Magnetic encoder or tone ring dirty, cracked or missing teeth
Worn or loose left front hub bearing changing the air gap

C0519.d: C0519 is the mechanical-fault code for the right front sensor. It appears in code lists, but no manufacturer publishes a setting rule for it; the known diagnostics put such faults under range, erratic or correlation codes.
s: ABS lamp and stability service message
ABS may regulate unexpectedly at walking pace
c: Metal debris or rust buildup on the right front reluctor ring
Sensor not fully seated or bracket bent, air gap too large

C051A.d: C051A names a mechanical fault at the left rear sensor. Like its siblings it is listed but not documented by any manufacturer, so the actual setting rule is unknown.
s: ABS lamp, sometimes only under load or on rough roads
Rear wheel speed drops out or jitters in live data
c: Rear tone ring bent or cracked, often after hub or brake work
Metal particles or rust on the rear encoder or sensor tip
Left rear hub bearing worn, encoder seal damaged

C051B.d: C051B covers a mechanical defect at the right rear wheel. No public manufacturer document defines when it is set; the cases known from bulletins carry other codes.
s: ABS, stability and traction lamps after rough stretches
Driver aids unavailable until the next ignition cycle
c: Right rear tone ring deformed or corroded
Right rear hub bearing loose or worn
Axle vibration disturbing the signal on rough surfaces

C051C.d: Module A delivers yaw rate and accelerations along several axes, but at least one channel sits outside what the vehicle's motion allows, for example a turn rate while parked or a lateral g that does not fit speed and steering. No manufacturer documents C051C publicly, so exact limits are unknown.
s: ESC or traction control warning lamp on
Stability control unavailable or intervening without reason
Yaw rate or acceleration not zero at standstill (scan tool)
c: Module A loose, tilted or mounted on a deformed bracket
Internal offset of the inertial sensor drifted beyond tolerance
Defective sensing element inside module A
Wrong module variant fitted or installed in the wrong orientation

C051D.d: The module holds no valid zero point or mounting orientation, typically after it or the brake controller was replaced and the setup step was skipped. Corrections like these live in non-volatile memory: Kelsey-Hayes measures the offset of the whole assembly on a turning stand and adds the in-car tilt.
s: ESC warning lamp on right after a repair
Stability and traction control unavailable
Driver assistance such as adaptive cruise may be disabled
c: Module A or brake control module replaced without configuration and yaw sensor learn
Learn procedure aborted, e.g. vehicle not level or voltage dropped
Stored calibration lost after software update or module fault

C051E.d: Module A's data arrive, but values jump, freeze briefly or vanish for short moments instead of changing smoothly. Modern units digitise yaw rate and accelerations inside the module and pass them on over a serial link: Bosch's SMI810 uses SafeSPI with 16-bit data, and a Hyundai/Kia design checks each value against the sensor's measuring range before sending it over CAN to the stability controller.
s: ESC warning lamp comes and goes
Stability control occasionally unavailable
Jumping yaw or acceleration values in live data
c: Loose or corroded connector at module A
Brief supply or ground dropouts, weak battery
Module not firmly fastened, picks up vibration
Sporadic internal fault of the sensor electronics

C051F.d: The brake controller finds that module A's signals do not agree with a second source of the same motion. Audi uses this code on the e-tron: the ABS unit (address 0003) stores C051F00, and Audi's 2019 bulletin names the suspension control module as sensor module A.
s: ESC warning lamp and several cluster messages
Yellow drive fault message (Audi e-tron)
Fault often gone after the next ignition cycle
c: ABS or suspension control software fault (Audi e-tron update)
Bus woken while modules enter sleep mode (door, charger)
Module A misaligned so its axes no longer match the reference
Fault in the comparison source (second inertial sensor, steering angle, wheel speeds)

C0520.d: General fault of module A without a narrower fault type. GM gives the most detail: in the 2023 and 2025 OBD tables of its Super Cruise controller (EOCM3), C0520 watches the high-performance IMU and sets when initialisation does not finish in time, the unit resets, its temperature status is invalid, offset or orientation learning is missing, or a swapped IMU is detected via its serial number.
s: ESC warning lamp or service message for stability control
Adaptive cruise or hands-free driving assistance unavailable (GM)
No check-engine lamp
c: IMU fails to initialise in time or resets during operation
Module swapped, offset or orientation calibration not learned
Software fault in the module or the receiving controller
Internal electronic failure of module A

C0521.d: Same fault type as C051C, but for a second inertial module B: its rates or accelerations lie outside what driving physics permits. No manufacturer explains C0521 publicly, and which unit is B on a given car is not documented either.
s: Driver assistance or ESC warning message
Adaptive cruise or lane functions unavailable
Module B reading not zero at standstill (scan tool)
c: Module B loose, tilted or bracket bent after a repair or impact
Bias of the accelerometers or gyros drifted out of tolerance
Defective sensing element inside module B

C0522.d: Module B lacks its stored zero point or installation data, so its readings cannot be trusted. No manufacturer publishes C0522, and which unit carries the letter B is not documented.
s: Warning message appears directly after a repair
Assistance or stability functions unavailable
c: Module B or its host control unit replaced without configuration
Vehicle variant or mounting position coded incorrectly
Calibration data lost after software update

C0523.d: Module B sends values that jump or drop out now and then. No manufacturer publishes C0523, so limits and the identity of module B stay open.
s: Assistance or ESC warning comes and goes
Code stored in history without current fault
Jumping values from module B in live data
c: Loose or corroded connector or ground at module B
Supply dips from a weak battery or poor connections
Sporadic internal fault in module B

C0524.d: Module B's readings disagree with another source for the same motion, most likely module A or values computed from steering angle and wheel speeds. No manufacturer publishes C0524; Audi documents only the A counterpart.
s: ESC or assistance warning message
Stability or assistance functions limited
c: Module A or B rotated on its mount after repair or impact
Drifting sensor in one of the two modules
Software or timing fault in the comparing controller

C0525.d: General fault of module B, without stating whether range, calibration, signal stability or correlation is at fault. No manufacturer publishes C0525, and the location of module B is not documented.
s: ESC, airbag-related or assistance warning depending on host module
Stability or assistance functions unavailable
c: Software fault, fixed by an update of the host module
Internal electronic failure of module B
Supply or ground fault at module B

C0526.d: C0526 is the base code for the steering angle sensor module, used when a fault is reported without a more specific failure type. MINI documents it for the 2017 Countryman F60 plug-in hybrid: an on-board diagnosis error in the electric power steering software stored C0526, readable only with a generic OBD tool, and lit the check-engine lamp.
s: Check-engine lamp on (MINI F60 PHEV)
ESC warning lamp on, stability control limited
c: Power steering software error (MINI F60 PHEV 2017)
Supply loss or battery disconnection without relearning
Internal fault in the steering angle sensor module

C0527.d: C0527 marks a mechanical rather than electrical fault of the steering angle sensor module. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: ESC warning lamp on
Angle on the scan tool jumps or stops changing while steering
Possible noise from the steering column
c: Worn or broken measuring gears inside the sensor
Sensor drive dog or mounting loose on the steering shaft
Sensor installed out of position after column or clock spring work

C0528.d: C0528 means the module delivers an angle that is out of range or behaves implausibly while it still communicates. Audi documents it on the 2015–2018 A3 e-tron as C052800, steering angle sender with implausible signal, sometimes stored together with P060700 after ESC had been switched off (TSB 2060682/1); the ESC lamp lights.
s: ESC warning lamp on
Stability control unavailable or intervening at odd moments
c: Steering angle sensor module delivering implausible values
ABS/ESC module software issue (Audi A3 e-tron)
Offset after alignment or steering work without re-zeroing

C0529.d: C0529 is set when the steering angle sensor module has no valid zero point. Stellantis documents it as C0529-00 on the 2023 Dodge Hornet and the 2023–2024 Alfa Romeo Tonale: if the wheel was turned without assist between key-off and key-on, the calibration was lost and the MIL came on, going out again after a lock-to-lock turn; an EPS software update fixes it (TSB 08-148-23, 08-163-23).
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on (Stellantis)
ESC warning lamp on, stability control limited until calibrated
Lamp goes out after turning the wheel from lock to lock
c: Calibration lost after battery disconnection or steering while switched off
Initialisation skipped after steering gear, sensor or alignment work

C052A.d: The steering angle sensor module reports wheel angle and turn rate to the stability control unit, which cross-checks that value against an independent estimate. Correlation means the reading and the estimate disagree for longer than the calibrated window; the signal itself is present.
s: ESC or traction control warning lamp on
Stability control switched off or intervening at the wrong moment
Steering wheel off-centre when driving straight
c: Angle offset after wheel alignment or steering work without zero-point adjustment
Internal fault in the steering angle sensor module
Faulty comparison signal (yaw rate, wheel speed or steering angle from power steering)

C052B.d: Range/performance fault of the ABS pump motor: the drive is commanded, but the motor or its relay does not behave as expected. On the 2023 Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV the brake unit maps C1051-04 (and C1051-49, added by bulletin TSB-23-35-002) to C052B; it is checked with normal supply voltage, set within 12 s; after a single trip the ASC, ABS and brake warnings plus the check-engine lamp come on.
s: ABS, ESC and brake warning lamps on
ABS and stability control unavailable, normal braking remains
No pump noise during the self-test after starting off
c: Pump motor worn (brushes) or pump seized in the hydraulic unit
Motor relay or switching stage in the ABS unit faulty
Marginal supply or ground connection under motor load

C052C.d: Open circuit in the ABS pump motor drive: the control unit finds no current path through motor or relay where one should exist. Mitsubishi lists C1051-13 as C052C on the 2023 Outlander PHEV within the same frame as C052B (normal supply, up to 12 s, ABS, ASC, brake and engine lamps after one trip, stability and regenerative braking functions off).
s: ABS and ESC warning lamps on
ABS, traction and stability control switched off
Code returns only after a short drive
c: Loose or corroded connector at the ABS unit
Worn brushes or open winding in the pump motor

C052D.d: The pump motor control circuit reads higher than the commanded state allows, which normally means the control line or motor terminal is shorted toward battery voltage or the switching stage is stuck on. No manufacturer publishes this code; Mitsubishi, for example, reports its pump motor faults under C052B and C052C.
s: ABS warning lamp on
Pump motor runs continuously or hums with ignition on
Battery discharged after standing
c: Motor relay or semiconductor switch in the ABS unit stuck closed
Motor lead or control line shorted to battery voltage
Moisture bridging pins in the ABS connector

C052E.d: Low counterpart of C052D: the pump motor control signal stays near ground when it should rise, pointing to a short to ground on the control side, a failed driver stage or a weak ground path of the hydraulic unit. No maker documents C052E publicly.
s: ABS and ESC warning lamps on
ABS and stability control unavailable
c: Poor ground connection of the ABS unit or hydraulic block
Control line or motor lead shorted to ground
Driver stage in the ABS control unit failed

C052F.d: The pump motor has its own battery feed, separate from the logic supply, and this code reports that feed as missing or open. Mitsubishi's 2023 Outlander PHEV manual shows the layout: motor and motor relay draw from a 60 A fusible link and must see 10–16 V at the unit connector, the valves from a separate 50 A link, the electronics from a 5 A fuse.
s: ABS and ESC warning lamps on
Pump motor never runs, ABS and stability control off
c: Pump motor fuse or fusible link blown
Corroded or loose battery feed terminal at the ABS connector
Open or high-resistance ground of the ABS unit

C0530.d: Plausibility fault of motor control A: the circuit is electrically intact, but the motor does not answer its command as the module expects – it stalls, runs too slowly or keeps turning. SAE J2012 lists the code in the chassis block beside the ABS pump motor and valve codes without naming the motor, and no manufacturer was found that publicly assigns it, so which drive counts as A stays open.
s: Chassis or brake warning lamp on
The function driven by motor A is unavailable
c: Motor or driven mechanism stiff or seized
Worn motor (brushes, bearings) delivering too little speed
Fault in the control unit's motor stage or feedback evaluation

C0531.d: Motor control A sees an open circuit: with the stage switched off, the module cannot detect the expected current path through the motor. J2012 names no specific motor and no public manufacturer assignment was found, so the actuator behind A depends on the vehicle.
s: Warning lamp of the affected system on
Motor A does not run at all
c: Connector to motor A unplugged or corroded
Broken motor lead in the harness
Open winding or worn brush in motor A

C0532.d: Motor control A reads high: a motor output sits near supply voltage although the driver commands it low or off. That points to a short to battery voltage in the motor leads or a high-side switch that no longer opens.
s: Warning lamp of the affected system on
Motor A runs on or gets hot
c: Motor lead chafed against a live wire
High-side switch in the control unit stuck on
Moisture bridging pins in the connector

C0533.d: Motor control A reads low: an output that should be driven up stays close to ground. Typical reasons are chafed motor wiring touching the body, water in a connector or a failed low-side stage; a stalled motor drawing excess current can look similar to the driver.
s: Warning lamp of the affected system on
Motor A does not start; a fuse may blow
c: Motor lead chafed through to body ground
Water ingress in the motor connector
Low-side stage in the control unit failed

C0534.d: The power feed of motor control A is missing or open, so the driver stage has nothing to switch even though the logic side of the module is alive. Chassis motors often get a dedicated battery feed: in the brake unit of the 2023 Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV, for example, the pump motor hangs on its own 60 A fusible link and needs 10–16 V at the connector.
s: Warning lamp of the affected system on
Motor A never runs while other functions of the module work
c: Fuse or fusible link of the motor feed blown
Open feed wire or loose supply terminal
Missing ground of the control unit's power stage

C0535.d: Second motor channel B fails its plausibility check: wiring and supply test fine, yet the motor's reaction to commands is wrong, for example too little speed, a delayed start or no stop. Where a controller drives two motors or two channels, A and B separate them; J2012 does not say which motor B is, and no manufacturer publicly assigns C0535, so the meaning must come from the vehicle's own service data.
s: Warning lamp of the affected system on
Function of motor B slow, incomplete or unavailable
c: Driven mechanism of motor B binding or blocked
Motor B worn and too slow
Faulty speed or position feedback in the control unit

C0536.d: Motor control B finds its load missing. The module expects a closed path through the windings of channel B and sees an open circuit instead – a pulled connector, a cut lead, corroded pins or an internal break in the motor.
s: Warning lamp of the affected system on
Motor B shows no reaction
c: Connector to motor B pulled off or pins corroded
Motor lead cut or broken in the harness
Internal break in motor B (winding, brush)

C0537.d: Channel B of the motor control reads high, meaning a motor terminal is pulled toward battery voltage against the command. A pinched lead touching a live wire, moisture bridging pins in a shared connector, or a high-side switch stuck in the conducting state are the usual suspects.
s: Warning lamp of the affected system on
Motor B runs on briefly or the function is switched off
c: Pinched motor B lead contacting a live wire
Moisture between pins of a shared connector
High-side switch for channel B not opening

C0538.d: Motor control B reads low: a channel-B output is held near ground. Besides a direct short of a motor lead to the body, the Bosch patent US5329238 also covers the case where both terminals deviate at once while driven, which it reads as a short across the motor itself or between its two lines.
s: Warning lamp of the affected system on
Motor B does not start
c: Motor B lead shorted to body near moving parts
Short across motor B or between its two lines
Water in the connector of motor B

C0539.d: Motor control B has lost its power supply, or the supply circuit is open. In many brake and chassis controllers the motor stage is fed by its own fused battery line while the logic runs from ignition, so the module can still communicate and store this code.
s: Warning lamp of the affected system on
Motor B never runs although the module communicates
c: Fuse or fusible link of the channel B feed open
Weak 12 V battery pulling the motor supply below the limit

C053A.d: The brake control unit holds no valid calibration for its ABS valves. Analog-controlled inlet valves open at a current that depends on the pressure difference, manufacturing scatter and wear, so the controller needs a stored opening-current curve to meter pressure finely.
s: ABS and ESC warning lamps on
ABS and stability control limited or switched off
c: ABS control unit or hydraulic unit replaced without valve calibration
Calibration run aborted (low voltage, air in the system, conditions not met)
Software update or memory fault erased the calibration data

C053B.d: Supply fault on the ABS solenoid valves: the feed that powers the inlet and outlet valves, usually switched through a valve relay inside the brake unit, is missing or open. On the 2023 Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV the code is C1048-11 (valve relay), shown as C053B; it is checked with normal supply, set within 2 s, and lights ASC, ABS, brake and check-engine lamps after one trip.
s: ABS, ESC and brake warning lamps on
ABS, stability control and electric parking brake functions unavailable
c: Valve relay inside the ABS unit faulty
Fusible link of the valve supply blown
Damaged or loose terminal in the ABS connector

C053C.d: A wheel speed signal is implausible, but the fault is reported generically rather than for one named wheel. Mitsubishi uses C106A-64 as C053C on the 2023 Outlander PHEV and runs four detection paths, one per sensor, each with a delay of at most 1 s; listed causes include the sensor, its rotor and a wrong tire size, and the code needs two trips before ASC, ABS, brake, parking brake and check-engine lamps light.
s: ABS, ESC and brake warning lamps on after two trips
ABS, traction control and stability control switched off
Speed-dependent assistance functions unavailable
c: Mismatched tire sizes or a space-saver spare fitted
Damaged or dirty encoder ring (sensor rotor)
Wheel speed sensor faulty or not seated correctly

C053D.d: The brake pressure sensor A signal is electrically present, but its value does not fit the braking situation. GM stores C053D in the brake system control module, calling it a circuit performance fault: on 2019 Silverado/Sierra 1500 drivers got a hard pedal plus the Service Brake Assist warning (PIT5638), and bulletin 20-NA-073 lists it among faults that drop the brake-by-wire system into its mechanical Push-Thru mode
s: Brake assist or stability control warning shown
Brake pedal hard or travelling further than usual
Check-engine lamp on some models
c: Brake or engine control software with an over-sensitive plausibility check (several bulletins)
Pressure and pedal sensors not initialized after module or hydraulic unit replacement
Air in the brake lines distorting the pressure build-up
Stop-light switch or pedal sensor delivering a mismatching reference
Drifting pressure sensor in the hydraulic unit

C053E.d: The voltage on the signal line of brake pressure sensor A has dropped under the lower limit the brake module accepts. Such ratiometric 5-V sensors normally stay within a window: an older Saab 9-5 brake unit faults its pressure sensor below 0.25 V held for 0.1 s.
s: ABS or stability control warning lamp lit
Message in the driver display right after start-up
Stability, traction control or brake assist switched off
c: Signal wire chafed through and touching ground
Missing or weak 5-V reference to the sensor
Module software flagging the sensor during start-up warm-up (GM HD trucks 2024)

C053F.d: Brake pressure sensor A reports a voltage above the upper limit of its valid band. Since the sensor is fed with 5 V, a short of the signal line to the reference or to battery voltage, a broken ground wire or an internal fault can push the reading up; a Saab 9-5 brake unit draws the line at 4.75 V lasting 0.1 s.
s: ABS and stability control warning lamps on
Traction control, stability control and hill-start assist unavailable
Check-engine lamp on some hybrids
c: Signal wire shorted to the 5-V reference or battery voltage
Pressure sensor in the hydraulic unit defective

C0540.d: General electrical fault in the circuit of brake pressure sensor A, typically an interrupted signal, reference or ground wire, or a connection with excessive resistance. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; Mitsubishi, for example, maps its sensor-A faults to C0044 and C053D to C053F instead.
s: ABS and ESC warning lamps on
Stability and traction control out of service
Brake assist or hill-start assist missing
c: Loose, corroded or pushed-out pin at the sensor or brake module connector
Broken signal, reference or ground wire
Internal open circuit in the pressure sensor

C0541.d: Brake pressure sensor B delivers a valid voltage, yet the value is implausible. Which sensor carries the letter B varies by maker.
s: Adaptive cruise control unavailable
ESC or ABS warning in the cluster
Assistance functions such as brake assist reduced
c: Pressure sensor inside the ESC hydraulic unit drifting or sluggish
Zero-point calibration not done after module or valve block replacement
Brake light switch or pedal sensor giving a contradictory reference

C0542.d: Brake pressure sensor B pulls its signal below the lowest voltage the receiving module treats as valid. Two makers name the code in public bulletins.
s: Check-engine or ESC warning lamp on
Adaptive cruise control or stop-start unavailable
c: Sensor or the ESC unit with integrated sensor defective
Engine control software misjudging the signal (Jeep Cherokee 2019)

C0543.d: Here the signal of brake pressure sensor B sits above the top of its permitted range, which points to a signal wire touching the 5-V reference or battery voltage, an open sensor ground, or a sensor that has failed high. Stellantis is the one maker naming the code publicly: bulletins covering the stop-start Cherokee of model year 2019 with the 3.2-litre V6 list Brake Pressure Sensor 2 Circuit High next to the matching
s: Check-engine lamp on
Stop-start or brake-related assistance not working
c: Signal wire shorted to reference or battery voltage
Sensor ground open or high resistance
Engine control software fault (Jeep Cherokee 2019 bulletins)
Sensor failed with permanently high output

C0544.d: The brake module sees a general electrical fault in the circuit of pressure sensor B, usually an interruption in signal, feed or ground. No maker publishes this exact meaning; note that GM bulletins use C0544 for a different, steering-related fault in its power steering module, so a GM scan result must be read with GM definitions.
s: ABS, traction and stability warning lamps on
Driver assistance relying on brake pressure unavailable
c: Connector at sensor or brake module loose or corroded
Interrupted signal, feed or ground wire
Open inside the sensor or the ESC unit carrying it

C0545.d: The brake system control module (BSCM) holds no vehicle identification number, or one that does not belong to the car it is fitted to. Modules store the VIN in non-volatile memory; GM patents describe a replacement module comparing its own stored VIN with the one held by another control unit and running a configuration routine when they differ, and point out that a swapped or tampered module shows up as a VIN discrep
s: ABS or ESC warning lamp on after a module replacement
Brake-related functions limited or disabled
c: New brake module installed without VIN programming
Used module from another vehicle still carrying its old VIN
Programming session interrupted, for example by low battery voltage

C0546.d: Generic variant without a named module: a chassis control unit reports that its stored vehicle identification number is blank or does not match the car. Which unit sets it is left to the maker, so the scan tool entry shows the module concerned.
s: Warning lamp of the affected chassis system on
Function of the replaced module missing or limited
c: Replacement chassis module not programmed with the vehicle VIN
Second-hand module carrying a foreign VIN
Software level not matching the vehicle configuration

C0547.d: Fault in the feed circuit powering the vacuum sensor on the brake booster, usually an open or a short on the regulated supply. Such sensors need a stable 5 V: HELLA specifies 4.5 to 5.5 V for its three-pin vacuum sensor (output, ground, supply), whose analogue signal tells the brake control unit when to run the electric vacuum pump.
s: Brake system or ESC warning shown
Stop-start inactive or electric vacuum pump running constantly
c: Supply wire or connector pin interrupted
Supply line shorted to ground or another circuit
Vacuum sensor shorting the supply internally

C0548.d: The supply reaching the vacuum sensor is present but sags below its lower limit. With a ratiometric sensor every output voltage scales with the feed, so an under-supplied sensor reports a wrong vacuum even if it is healthy.
s: Brake or ESC warning lamp on
Vacuum reading implausible in live data
Further codes for sensors on the same supply
c: Another sensor on the same 5-V rail drawing it down
Corroded contact or damaged feed wire adding resistance
Weak sensor supply output in the control module

C0549.d: General circuit fault of vacuum sensor A, usually a broken or disconnected signal, ground or feed line. The sensor measures the vacuum in the brake booster; Bosch notes that its value lets the system run the electric vacuum pump, permits engine stop-start and supports ESP functions.
s: Brake assist warning or ABS lamp on
Stop-start no longer switching off the engine
c: Sensor plug loose or not latched after work in the engine bay
Broken signal, ground or supply wire
Internal open in the vacuum sensor

C054A.d: Vacuum sensor A delivers an in-range voltage that does not agree with what the booster should hold. Patents show the logic: GM compares booster vacuum with engine vacuum from the MAP sensor while the throttle is closed, because the two should track each other without braking, and flags a sensor biased high or low when the difference persists too long; Ford relies on the check valve and treats a booster pressure clear
s: Brake assist warning or reduced assist feel
Electric vacuum pump running more often than normal
Stop-start or cylinder deactivation inhibited
c: Vacuum sensor drifted or contaminated (oil, moisture)
Real leak in hose, check valve or booster making the reading look wrong
Faulty comparison value, such as manifold pressure

C054B.d: The signal of vacuum sensor A has fallen below the lowest voltage a working sensor can produce. In HELLA's design the output runs from 0.5 V at no vacuum to 4.5 V at −1000 hPa and is clamped to a 0.4–4.8 V band, so anything under that floor must be electrical: a grounded signal line, an absent 5-V feed or an internally failed sensor.
s: Brake assist or brake system warning lit
Electric vacuum pump running continuously
c: Sensor failed with output stuck low

C054C.d: Vacuum sensor A reports a voltage above its upper clamp. HELLA's booster sensor never exceeds 4.8 V when intact, even at full vacuum, so a higher reading indicates a signal shorted to the 5-V supply or to battery voltage, an open ground, or an internal defect.
s: Brake assist warning on
Harder brake pedal if the booster really runs short of vacuum
c: Signal line shorted to supply or battery voltage
Sensor failed with output stuck high

C054D.d: Circuit fault on a second vacuum sensor, labelled B, typically an open in its signal, ground or feed. Some systems carry more than one vacuum measurement, for example a booster sensor next to one on the pump or supply line, but which sensor is B is not published by any maker, and no manufacturer documents C054D.
s: Brake system or brake assist warning
Vacuum pump control in fallback, pump running longer
c: Connector of sensor B unplugged, loose or corroded
Interrupted wire in the sensor harness

C054E.d: Sensor B reports a plausible-looking voltage, but the vacuum it represents contradicts the expected value. With two vacuum sensors a module can also compare them with each other; publicly, the comparison methods come from patents on booster sensors: Ford treats booster pressure lying clearly above manifold pressure as sensor degradation, since a working check valve prevents that state, and checks whether booster pres
s: Brake assist or brake system warning
Pedal feels firmer after several brake applications
c: Leak, faulty check valve or weak vacuum pump
Wrong sensor type fitted after repair

C054F.d: The voltage from vacuum sensor B is lower than any value its characteristic allows. Taking HELLA's booster sensor as the reference, the output should never drop below 0.4 V, while 0.5 V corresponds to no vacuum at all; a reading underneath that is electrical rather than physical.
s: Brake assist warning shown
Stop-start unavailable
c: Signal wire of sensor B grounded
Output stage of sensor B failed

C0550.d: Vacuum sensor B puts out more voltage than its design permits. HELLA caps the output of its booster sensor at 4.8 V, with 4.5 V already standing for −1000 hPa, so anything above is a wiring or sensor fault: signal touching the supply or battery voltage, a broken ground return or a failed sensor.
s: Brake assist or brake system warning on
Firm pedal possible if the pump is not switched on when needed
c: Signal of sensor B shorted to supply or battery voltage
Ground return of sensor B broken
Sensor B stuck at high output

C0551.d: C0551 reports an electrical break in the longitudinal acceleration sensor circuit: the brake or stability module no longer gets a usable fore-aft signal, usually because the signal or supply wire is open or a plug has lost contact. Earlier layouts mounted a separate g-sensor close to the centre of gravity and cabled it to the ABS unit; a Kelsey-Hayes patent (now ZF) describes a capacitive element whose analog voltage
s: ABS and/or ESC warning lamp on
Stability, traction or hill-start assistance unavailable
ABS on four-wheel-drive vehicles regulates less precisely
c: Broken signal or supply wire between sensor and brake module
Corroded, loose or pushed-back terminal at the sensor plug
Internal open in the sensor or, on integrated designs, in the ABS/ESC unit

C0552.d: Here the fore-aft acceleration signal arrives but does not match how the car is actually moving. Mitsubishi's 2023 Outlander PHEV brake controller reports its built-in decel G sensor fault C1071-64 as C0552; the check needs a healthy supply and takes up to 2 s, and a second faulty drive turns on the ASC and ABS warnings as well as the check-engine lamp.
s: ESC/ASC and ABS warning lamps on, MIL possible on some models
Stability control, traction control and hill start assist switched off
Fault returns after load or tyre changes
c: Changed vehicle attitude, e.g. different tyre sizes front and rear or overload
ABS/ESC unit or sensor mounted at the wrong angle or loose
Sensor offset drifted or internal sensor defect
Faulty wheel speed data used as comparison value

C0553.d: C0553 is stored when the longitudinal acceleration signal sits below the lowest voltage the module accepts. Analog acceleration sensors idle at mid-scale; a Hyundai/Kia patent gives 2.5 V as the zero point of a G-sensor on a 5 V reference, so a level dragged toward 0 V cannot come from real braking but points to the wiring: signal shorted to ground, missing sensor supply, or a sensor whose output stage has failed.
s: ESC and ABS warning lamps on from start-up
Stability control and hill-hold unavailable
c: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Sensor reference supply missing or collapsed
Sensor output stage failed at the lower end

C0554.d: C0554 is the upper counterpart of C0553: the fore-aft acceleration voltage stays above the highest value that a real sensor reading may take. With a mid-scale zero point, as in a Hyundai/Kia G-sensor patent (2.5 V on a 5 V supply), a value pinned near the reference voltage would mean an absurd, constant acceleration, so the module treats it as a circuit fault.
s: ESC and ABS warning lamps on
Traction and stability assistance switched off
c: Signal wire shorted to a supply voltage
Moisture or corrosion bridging pins in the sensor connector
Sensor output stage failed at the upper end

C0555.d: The left front wheel speed signal is present, but the ABS module concludes that the part behind it is not the one it expects. Mitsubishi maps its code C1061-4A on the 2023 Outlander PHEV to C0555 and defines it as the front left sensor fitted in the wrong position; the module needs no more than 3 s to flag it, provided the sensor supply is intact, and the second affected drive brings on the MIL together with the ASC
s: ABS and ESC/ASC warning lamps on after a sensor or hub repair
Check-engine lamp on some models
Electric parking brake and hill descent control unavailable
c: Wrong sensor variant fitted (other side, other axle or passive instead of active)
Sensors or their connectors swapped between wheel positions
ABS control unit misjudges a correct sensor

C0556.d: Mirror of C0555 for the right front wheel: the sensor delivers pulses, yet the ABS module rejects it as the wrong component. Mitsubishi lists its code C1063-4A on the 2023 Outlander PHEV as C0556, with the same rule (fitted at the wrong position, at most 3 s, two trips to MIL plus ASC and ABS lamps).
s: ABS and stability warning lamps on, MIL on some models
No ABS or ESC intervention on slippery roads
c: Replacement sensor of the wrong type (passive instead of active, other side)
Stored code left over because no test drive followed the repair

C0557.d: C0557 concerns the speed sensor at the left rear wheel: its signal exists, but the ABS module judges the fitted part as not matching. Mitsubishi lists C1065-4A on the 2023 Outlander PHEV as C0557 (sensor in the wrong position, up to 3 s, MIL after two trips).
s: Several brake system warnings at start-up
ABS and stability control unavailable
Check-engine lamp on some models
c: ABS module software misjudges the sensor (fixed by reprogramming)
Wrong or other-side sensor fitted at the left rear
Rear sensor connectors swapped left and right

C0558.d: For the right rear wheel, C0558 says the ABS module does not accept the installed speed sensor as the correct part. Mitsubishi maps C1067-4A on the 2023 Outlander PHEV to C0558 (wrong installation position, detection within 3 s, MIL after two trips).
s: Yellow or red ABS warning indicator on
Stability and traction control switched off
Check-engine lamp on some models
c: Wrong sensor variant fitted at the right rear
Sensor or harness damaged by brake heat

C0559.d: C0559 covers the rear steering controller, the electronics of active rear-wheel steering, when it fails its own performance or plausibility checks. Systems such as ZF's AKC turn the rear wheels by up to 12° opposite to the front ones at low speed and in the same direction from about 60 km/h.
s: Steering or rear steering warning in the instrument cluster
Larger turning circle, rear wheels held straight
Driver assistance functions limited on some models
c: Rear steering control module software fault (update available)
Disagreeing position or angle signals inside the rear steering actuator
Poor ground or supply of the rear steering unit
Damaged, contaminated or worn rear steering actuator

C055A.d: Supply voltage A of the ABS pump motor is above its upper limit. The motor draws heavy current, so overvoltage stresses motor, relay or semiconductor switch; typical causes are a faulty alternator regulator, a jump-start or charger at too high a voltage, or a measuring fault in the module.
s: ABS and ESC warning lamps on
Other overvoltage warnings or flickering lights at the same time
c: Alternator regulator or DC/DC converter delivering too high a voltage
Jump-start or battery charger with excessive voltage
Voltage measurement fault in the ABS control unit

C055B.d: Supply voltage A of the pump motor is below its lower limit. Under load the motor pulls the feed down, so a weak 12 V battery, a corroded terminal, a high-resistance fusible link or a poor ground can all set it, and the relay may chatter.
s: ABS and ESC warning lamps on, often after cold starts
Pump runs sluggishly or ABS functions drop out
c: Corroded terminal or high-resistance fusible link in the motor feed
Poor ground connection of the ABS unit

C055C.d: The return pump motor of the ABS/ESC hydraulic unit has its own power feed, usually a fused line from the battery switched through a relay or a transistor stage in the module. C055C means this feed is present but its voltage does not behave as expected while the motor is off or running – sagging under load, slow to rise or drifting – as opposed to the hard open or short codes C052F, C055A and C055B.
s: ABS and stability control warning lamps on
No pump buzz during the start-up self-test
Normal braking remains, but without ABS regulation
c: Corroded or loose pump motor fuse, feed terminal or ground at the hydraulic unit
Weak battery or charging fault letting the supply collapse under motor load
Worn or sticking pump motor drawing excessive current
Faulty motor relay or driver stage inside the ABS module

C055D.d: Passenger-car brakes are split into two hydraulic circuits so that one can still stop the car if the other fails. Brake-by-wire units with a motor-driven plunger can estimate fluid loss directly: they compare the plunger travel with the measured pressure.
s: Red brake warning and amber ABS or stability lamp
Soft or sinking brake pedal, longer stopping distance
Falling fluid level or wet spots at a wheel
c: Leaking brake line, hose, fitting or caliper in this circuit
Worn seal in the master cylinder or the brake-by-wire unit
Air left in the circuit after service, read as compliance or leakage
Overly sensitive leak calculation in the brake module software

C055E.d: C055E reports a leak in hydraulic circuit A, the counterpart of C055D. Land Rover documents it on the Defender L663 from 2020 as C055E-7A, meaning lost fluid or a failed seal, with amber ABS and DSC lamps.
s: Amber ABS and DSC/ESC lamps, possibly red brake warning
Longer pedal travel or spongy feel
Warning returns after clearing until the self-check passes
c: Fluid escaping from a line, hose, union or caliper of circuit A
Internal seal failure in master cylinder or hydraulic unit
Repair done but the required self-check was not completed, so the code stays
Air trapped after bleeding or component replacement

C055F.d: The brake system control module (BSCM) or electronic brake boost controller (EBBC) has found that its hydraulic unit – master cylinder, pedal simulator, separation valves or boost plunger – does not perform as calculated. GM's 2019 tables test it during shutdown: a simulator leak sets C055F if secondary pressure drops under 15 bar; in 2025 a master cylinder leakage above 200 mm³/s also counts, Type A with MIL.
s: Service Brake System message, ABS and stability lamps
Hard pedal or changed brake pedal effort
Check-engine lamp on some models
c: Internal leak or failure of the master cylinder or pedal simulator
Low battery voltage, especially in severe cold, during the self-test
Brake module software flagging the unit too readily (update available)
Poor power or ground terminals at the brake module

C0560.d: The brake module expects stored calibration data for pressure sensor A, normally the master cylinder pressure sensor: zero offset, sensor identity and a flag that the end-of-line or service calibration succeeded. C0560 means this data is absent or does not match the fitted sensor.
s: ABS, traction or stability lamp on after brake repair
Brake assist or stability functions unavailable
Check-engine lamp on some GM models
c: Pressure sensor calibration skipped after replacing the brake module or hydraulic unit
Calibration interrupted, e.g. pedal touched or voltage dropped during the routine
Used or wrong hydraulic unit whose sensor data do not match the module
Non-volatile memory error in the brake module

C0561.d: Where two vacuum signals describe the brake booster supply, the module expects them to track each other; C0561 means sensor A and sensor B disagree beyond the allowed band. No maker documents this code number publicly.
s: Brake or stability warning lamp
Electric vacuum pump runs too often or not at all
Stop/start or brake assist unavailable on some cars
c: One vacuum sensor drifting or reading offset
Leaking or kinked vacuum hose or check valve between the two measuring points
Corroded connector or damaged wiring on one sensor
Unstable 5 V reference or ground shared by the sensors

C0562.d: Hybrids, EVs and brake-by-wire cars measure how hard the driver wants to brake with a contactless pedal angle or travel sensor. Bosch builds these with a magnetic field sensor on a 5 V supply and two redundant outputs, often pulse-width modulated, so the module can cross-check them.
s: Brake system or ABS warning lamp
Regenerative braking reduced or off, pedal feel changes
Brake lights or cruise control affected on some cars
c: Broken 5 V supply wire or pin pushed out at the pedal sensor
Sensor connector loose or left unplugged after pedal-area work
Internal open circuit in the pedal sensor
Brake module no longer providing the 5 V reference

C0563.d: C0563 is a summary code: the ABS control module reports that it cannot carry out its own function correctly, without pinning the fault on one sensor or valve. Ford shows how it is used.
s: Check Brake System message and ABS lamp
ABS and stability control unavailable
Regenerative braking limited on hybrids
c: Air in the hydraulic system or brake service mode left active after work
Internal ABS module fault or corrupted memory
Outdated or incomplete module software or configuration
Unstable supply or ground at the ABS module

C0564.d: The ABS module needs a stable 12 V supply to switch its valves and pump. C0564 means its measured system voltage has dropped below the permitted minimum.
s: ABS, stability and brake warnings, often together with other modules' warnings
Electric parking brake or hill hold unavailable
Warnings disappear after recharging the battery
c: Weak or deeply discharged 12 V battery
High resistance in the module fuse, feed wire or ground
Alternator or DC/DC converter not supplying enough voltage
Parasitic drain or aftermarket equipment pulling the battery down

C0565.d: C0565 is set when the ABS module measures a supply voltage above its permitted maximum; excess voltage can damage the valve and pump drivers, so the module stops regulating. Mitsubishi maps its C1056-17 to C0565 on the 2023 Outlander PHEV: 16 V or more on the ignition feed within 1 s, ASC, ABS, brake and parking brake lamps plus the MIL after two trips; ABS, EBD, ASC, brake assist and the electric parking brake are s
s: ABS, stability, brake and parking brake warnings
Check-engine lamp on some models
Bulbs burning out or other modules reporting overvoltage
c: Faulty alternator regulator or DC/DC converter overcharging the 12 V system
Jump-start or battery charger set to an excessive voltage
Poor ground making the module read voltage too high

C0566.d: Some vacuum brake boosters carry an electrically operated valve that lets air into the working chamber without pedal input – for emergency brake assist or, on hybrids, to blend friction and regenerative braking. An Aisin patent shows the idea: when energised, the solenoid admits atmospheric pressure to an auxiliary chamber and raises boost.
s: Brake system or stability warning
Brake assist or regenerative blending unavailable
Pedal feel changes on hybrids
c: Solenoid connector loose, unlatched or corroded at the booster
Broken wire between ABS module and booster solenoid
Open solenoid coil inside the booster

C0567.d: C0567 flags the brake booster solenoid circuit as too low – typically a short to ground on the line between the module's high-side driver and the coil. Ford describes the check in its 2015–2019 hybrid summaries: with both high-side and low-side drivers switched off, the module measures the voltage on the solenoid supply; below 3.0 V for 380 ms the fault is stored, and Ford's hybrid powertrain module shows it as C0567
s: Brake system warning lamp
No automatic brake assist
Less regenerative braking on hybrids
c: Chafed solenoid wire shorting to body ground
Moisture or corrosion bridging the connector pins
Shorted solenoid winding inside the booster

C0568.d: C0568 is the high-side counterpart of C0567: the solenoid circuit carries voltage when it should be dead. In Ford's 2015–2019 hybrid logic both drivers are commanded off and the solenoid supply line must stay near zero; more than 3.0 V for 80 ms points to a short to battery voltage or a driver that will not switch off, and the hybrid powertrain module reports C0568 (ABS code C0022).
s: Brake system warning lamp
Brake assist switched off
Unusual pedal feel on hybrids
c: Solenoid wire chafed against a powered circuit
High-side driver in the ABS module not switching off
Contamination bridging pins in the solenoid connector

C0569.d: C0569 covers booster solenoid faults that are neither a clear open nor a clean short: the circuit reacts, but not as the module expects. Ford's hybrids (2015–2019) run three checks during operation, each over 80 ms: more than 2 V over the low-side driver while the high side is off, less than 160 mA in the test pulse with the high side on, or under 3.0 V supply with the high side on.
s: Intermittent brake system warning
Brake assist occasionally unavailable
Code returns after clearing
c: Corroded or loose terminals adding resistance in the solenoid circuit
Degraded driver stage in the ABS module

C056A.d: Pressure sensors in the brake system are ratiometric parts fed with 5 V from the control module; HELLA's booster vacuum sensor, for example, is specified for 4.5–5.5 V and answers with 0.5–4.5 V. If that supply is missing or out of range, every reading is wrong, so C056A is checked before the sensor signals are judged.
s: Brake or stability warning, often with further sensor codes
Brake assist or electric vacuum pump control affected
Stop/start inactive on some cars
c: Open or shorted 5 V supply wire to the sensor
Another sensor on the same reference pulling the supply down
Faulty 5 V regulator in the control module

C056B.d: C056B means the signal from brake pressure sensor A drops out or jumps for short moments instead of being steadily wrong. Ford's hybrid summaries (2015–2019) name two triggers: a checksum error in the digital data coming from the sensor for 70 ms, or a commanded control signal that does not show up at the sensor within 70 ms; the check runs only with a healthy sensor supply (no C056A).
s: ABS and stability lamps that come and go
Stability control or hill start assist off until next start
Regenerative braking reduced on hybrids
c: Loose or corroded contact in the pressure sensor connector or harness
Disturbed digital sensor line, e.g. damaged shielding or poor ground
Sensor electronics failing intermittently, often in the hydraulic unit
Brief dips in the 5 V sensor supply

C056C.d: C056C is the intermittent fault of the second brake pressure sensor, B. Which pressure B measures depends on the system – in Ford's hybrid ABS modules the two sensors read different points of the hydraulic unit, and other makers fit sensor B in a separate circuit or in the boost chamber.
s: Sporadic ABS or stability warning
Traction and stability control briefly unavailable
No noticeable change in normal braking
c: Intermittent contact at the sensor B connector or harness
Sensor B electronics dropping out under heat or vibration
Poor ground or unstable reference voltage

C056D.d: The brake pedal angle sensor of a hybrid or brake-by-wire car is fed from a regulated 5 V line. C056D means this supply is present but sagging.
s: Brake system warning and possibly stability lamp
Regenerative braking reduced, firmer friction braking
On GM models parking brake messages instead
c: Pedal sensor loading the supply through an internal fault
Supply wire chafed to ground near the pedal box
Another sensor on the same 5 V rail pulling it down
Weak 5 V regulator in the brake module

C056E.d: C056E is stored when the 5 V feed of the brake pedal position sensor rises above its limit. In Ford's 2015–2019 hybrid logic that means more than 5.13 V for 50 ms; the ABS module records C100F and the hybrid powertrain module C056E.
s: Brake system warning lamp
Regenerative braking limited
Pedal sensor plausibility codes may follow
c: Supply wire shorted to a battery-voltage circuit
Open sensor ground letting the reference float high
Faulty 5 V regulator in the brake module

C056F.d: The travel sensor tells the booster control how far its input side has moved. On older vacuum boosters it followed the movable wall; on Bosch's iBooster a differential travel sensor measures the offset between the pedal-driven input rod and the motor-driven booster body, and the controller works to bring that offset back to zero.
s: Hard brake pedal with clearly higher pedal force
Brake system or stability warning lamp and a message to service the brakes
Brake assist, automatic emergency braking or regenerative braking unavailable
c: Travel sensor signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Missing 5 V supply to the sensor, e.g. corroded connector pin at the booster
Internal fault of the travel sensor, usually built into the booster assembly
Defective sensor input stage in the booster control unit

C0570.d: C0570 is the high-side counterpart of C056F: the booster travel signal reads above its plausible maximum. Typical triggers are a signal wire touching the 5 V reference line or battery positive, or a broken sensor ground that lets the input float upward.
s: Electric brake assist switched off, pedal much harder
Brake warning and stability control lamp on
Driver assistance braking functions disabled
c: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference or to battery voltage
Open sensor ground letting the signal float to the upper limit
Travel sensor damaged internally, e.g. after water ingress at the booster
Wrong or not properly installed booster or sensor after a repair

C0571.d: Brake pressure sensor C is an additional hydraulic pressure sensor whose job depends on the brake system; each maker assigns the letter itself. GM uses C0571 in three variants.
s: Check engine light together with ABS or stability warning (GM)
Regenerative braking or brake assist reduced, pedal feel changed
Brake pressure reading on the scan tool stuck at its minimum
c: Sensor signal line shorted to ground in the harness or connector
Sensor supply missing, so the output stays at its lowest value
Defective pressure sensor, often integrated in the hydraulic or brake module

C0572.d: C0572 marks the upper end of the same sensor C channel: the pressure signal is at or above its top limit. GM's 2016–2019 hybrid brake modules check the signal voltage against the supply voltage and set the code when the two are practically equal for 0.1 s.
s: Check engine light plus ABS or stability lamp (GM)
Scan tool shows high brake pressure with the pedal released
Brake assist and regenerative braking restricted
c: Signal line shorted to the 5 V reference or another supply
Open signal line pulled high by the module input (GM counts this here)
Pressure sensor reporting full scale because of an internal fault

C0573.d: C0573 is reserved for an interrupted circuit of brake pressure sensor C – a broken signal, supply or ground wire, or a connector that has lost contact. No manufacturer documents it publicly; GM, which uses C0571 and C0572 for this sensor, books an open signal line under C0572.
s: ABS, stability or brake warning lamp on
Pressure value missing or fixed at a rail on the scan tool
Fault may come and go when the connector is moved
c: Loose, corroded or pushed-back pin at the sensor or module connector
Broken signal, supply or ground wire in the harness
Internal open circuit in the pressure sensor

C0574.d: Here the sensor C signal is electrically within limits but does not make sense. GM's 2016–2019 hybrid brake modules learn the zero point while the pedal is released and set C0574 if the offset exceeds ±1,500 kPa; to confirm a repair the car is driven at about 37 mph for 5 s without braking.
s: Check engine light and ABS or stability lamp (GM)
Uneven or changed braking feel when regeneration blends in
Code returns after clearing once the car has been driven
c: Pressure sensor zero point drifted with age or temperature
Residual pressure while learning, e.g. dragging pedal or sticking valve
Poor sensor ground shifting the signal level
Sensor values not relearned after replacing the brake module

C0575.d: Brake pressure sensor D is a further hydraulic pressure sensor whose position is set by the manufacturer. In GM's hybrid brake control modules of 2016–2019 it measures brake pressure at the left rear wheel, and C0575 is stored when its signal stays under 0.3 V for 0.1 s while the ignition is on, rated Type A with MIL after one trip.
s: Check engine light with brake or stability warning (GM hybrids)
Regenerative braking reduced, more friction braking
Rear pressure reading near zero even when braking
c: Signal line of sensor D shorted to ground
Sensor supply interrupted, output drops to near 0 V

C0576.d: C0576 is set when the signal of brake pressure sensor D sits too high. GM's 2016–2019 hybrid brake tables, where D is the left rear wheel pressure sensor, compare the signal line against the supply: a level over 3.3 V lasting 0.1 s at ignition on stores the code, Type A with MIL after one trip.
s: Check engine light and brake warnings (GM hybrids)
High rear pressure shown with the pedal released
Less regenerative braking, ABS/ESC restricted
c: Signal line shorted to the 5 V reference or to battery voltage
Open sensor ground, signal floats high
Sensor internally damaged, reports maximum pressure

C0577.d: C0577 stands for an open circuit of brake pressure sensor D. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Brake, ABS or stability warning lamp
No valid value for sensor D on the scan tool
Regenerative braking or brake assist limited
c: Connector of sensor D unplugged, corroded or with a spread terminal
Wire broken near the sensor, e.g. at a flex point toward the rear axle
Internal open circuit in sensor D

C0578.d: For sensor D the range/performance check targets a signal that is electrically fine but implausible. In GM's 2016–2019 hybrid brake modules, where D measures left rear brake pressure, the zero offset is learned while the car is being driven above about 4.5 mph with the brake released and the hydraulic pump idle; an offset beyond ±1,500 kPa sets C0578 at once, Type A with MIL.
s: Check engine light and brake warnings (GM hybrids)
Rear brake pressure shown although no brake is applied
Code sets again after a short drive
c: Zero point of sensor D drifted
Pressure trapped in the rear circuit, e.g. sticking caliper or valve
Ground offset between sensor and brake module

C0579.d: Electromechanical brake boosters watch the heat in their motor and power electronics so they can scale back assist before damage; a Hitachi Astemo patent, for example, describes one sensor on the motor and one in the drive circuit, with assist limited above set temperatures. GM reads two temperature channels from its booster: A under P25C6/P25C7, B under C0579/C057A.
s: Check engine light after two trips (GM 2023/2025), brake warning
Brake assist may be reduced as a precaution
Booster temperature B shows an implausible value on the scan tool
c: Temperature signal B shorted to ground inside the booster or its harness
Fault in the booster control electronics reading the channel

C057A.d: C057A is the high counterpart: temperature channel B of the booster reads at its upper end, which GM interprets as the signal shorted to supply. GM's 2023 and 2025 EBCM tables set it above 3.14 V when five checks in a row fail within 0.6 s and rate it Type B, with MIL after two trips; the 2019 Cadillac XT4 version uses 3.34 V and is Type C without MIL.
s: Check engine light after two trips (GM 2023/2025) and brake warning
Temperature B reading stuck at a limit
Reduced brake assist during long downhill braking
c: Temperature signal B shorted to the sensor supply or another voltage
Thermistor or its return line open, pulling the input to the rail
Moisture or corrosion inside the booster electronics

C057B.d: C057B is defined for an interrupted circuit of booster temperature sensor B. No manufacturer publishes it; GM maps the faults of this channel to C0579 and C057A only.
s: Brake system warning and service message
Temperature B missing or at an extreme value on the scan tool
Assist possibly limited to protect the motor
c: Open wire or loose pin between thermistor and booster electronics
Cracked thermistor body or broken lead after thermal or mechanical stress
Failed solder joint on the booster circuit board

C057C.d: C057C covers a temperature B value that is electrically valid but behaves implausibly – it stays frozen, climbs too slowly after hard use, or departs from what the module's thermal estimate predicts. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Brake warning, often after long or repeated braking
Temperature B frozen or lagging behind temperature A
Assist reduced earlier than usual
c: Thermistor resistance drifted through age, moisture or heat cycling
Sensor lost thermal contact with motor or power stage
Plausibility model in the booster software too strict

C057D.d: C057D is meant for a temperature B signal that drops out or jumps for brief moments instead of failing for good – a loose connector pin, a cracked solder joint or a wire breaking under vibration are the classic reasons. No manufacturer publishes a threshold for it.
s: Brake warning that appears and disappears
Temperature B jumping on the scan tool
Code returns some time after clearing
c: Loose or fretting pin in the booster connector
Cracked solder joint of the thermistor on the circuit board
Moisture ingress causing leakage currents at the sensor

C057E.d: With two temperature sensors in the booster the module can cross-check them: after a long rest both should be close to ambient, and under load they should move in a consistent pattern. C057E is set when sensors A and B disagree beyond a plausible margin.
s: Brake system warning with service message
Temperatures A and B clearly apart on the scan tool after a cold start
Reduced brake assist
c: One of the two thermistors drifted or lost thermal contact
Added resistance in one sensor circuit, e.g. corroded contact
Real local overheating of motor or power stage, e.g. after jammed mechanics

C057F.d: C057F covers an interrupted drive path in the three-phase motor of an electric brake booster: a winding, a phase lead or a power transistor that no longer carries current. GM documents it in several brake modules, always as Type A with MIL after one trip.
s: Hard brake pedal, noticeably more pedal force needed
Brake system, ABS/traction and check engine lamps on
Message about reduced brake assist
c: Broken winding or failed internal phase connection in booster motor A
Bridge transistor in the brake module no longer switching (drive stage defect)
Corroded or loose phase contact between control unit and motor, raising coil resistance

C0580.d: C0580 flags a phase of booster motor A that is pulled too low, or a driver stage that cannot lift it properly. GM's 2016 and 2019 hybrid tables use it when the gate-drive supply of the bridge driver falls too far below the motor supply (7 V limit, 5 ms).
s: Electric brake assist off, pedal feels hard
Brake and stability warning lamps, on GM also the check engine lamp
Fault may appear right after switching the ignition on
c: Phase lead of motor A chafed through and shorted to ground
Gate-driver or charge-pump supply in the brake module too low (internal defect or weak supply)
Lower bridge transistor shorted or permanently driven

C0581.d: C0581 is reserved for a phase of booster motor A whose voltage sits too high – typically a phase lead touching battery positive or an upper power transistor that stays conductive. No manufacturer publishes C0581: GM's brake tables list only C057F, C0580 and C0582 for the phase circuits of this motor, and its 2019 IBC unit books stuck-high phases under C057F.
s: Brake assist switched off, high pedal effort
Brake system warning lamp and service message
c: Phase lead of motor A shorted to battery voltage
Upper bridge transistor in the brake module shorted or stuck on
Moisture in the booster connector creating a leakage path to supply

C0582.d: C0582 is the plausibility check of the drive stage for booster motor A and the best documented code of this group. GM's 2016/2019 hybrid tables switch an upper and a lower transistor of different phases in all six pairings and trip above 150 A; the 2023/2025 EBCM tables expect an idle phase at 1.65 V during start-up and also file a temperature-sensor plausibility test here.
