s: Check engine, traction control and ABS lamps on together
Brake assist failure message, abnormal pedal feel
Reduced assist especially during hard or panic braking
c: Software fault in the brake system control module (GM 22-NA-100, fixed by reprogramming)
Defective bridge driver or shorted transistor pair in the drive stage
Internal fault of the eBooster unit, requiring booster and module replacement

C0583.d: C0583 refers to the second motor or second winding system, B, of an electric brake booster and reports an interrupted phase path there. Not every booster has a B side: GM's public tables diagnose motor A only, and no manufacturer documents C0583 in this meaning.
s: Brake warning lamp with a service message
Weaker or slower brake assist if only side A remains
c: Open winding or internal phase connection of motor/winding system B
Power module B with a transistor that no longer conducts
Loose or corroded phase contact on the B side

C0584.d: C0584 means a phase of booster motor B is held too low – shorted to ground, a lower transistor that will not switch off, or a driver whose gate supply has collapsed. No manufacturer publishes the code in its booster meaning; it shows up only in GM's older keyword list (PIP5094), where the number belonged to another system.
s: Brake system warning and possibly reduced assist
Driver assistance braking functions may be limited
c: Phase lead of side B shorted to ground or housing
Lower transistor of power module B shorted
Gate-driver supply of channel B too low

C0585.d: C0585 stands for a phase of booster motor B reading too high, for instance a lead shorted to battery positive or an upper transistor stuck on. The number had another use on older GM-platform cars: on the 2011 Saab 9-5 it identified the left rear damper actuator of the adaptive suspension.
s: Brake system warning lamp
Reduced or switched-off electric assist
c: Phase lead of side B shorted to battery voltage
Upper transistor of power module B shorted or stuck on
Code read on an older GM-platform vehicle where C0585 belongs to a damper actuator

C0586.d: C0586 is set when the B drive stage of the booster motor is electrically connected but behaves implausibly: phase currents that do not match the command, a transistor pair conducting at once, or a bridge driver that fails its start-up self-test. Nobody publishes limits for side B.
s: Brake warning or service message
Pedal response weaker or slower than usual
c: Bridge driver of channel B failing its self-test
Current measurement of channel B drifting, currents no longer match the command
Control unit software issue, resolved by update where available

C0587.d: C0587 concerns the rotor position sensor of booster motor A – a resolver, a sine/cosine magnetic sensor or a set of Hall elements that tells the controller where the rotor stands so it can commutate the windings. The code reports an open sensor circuit.
s: Electric brake assist reduced or off, hard pedal
Brake warning lamp and message
c: Broken signal or supply wire of the position sensor
Pushed-back or corroded pin at the sensor or module connector
Sensor element inside the booster failed, booster unit usually replaced

C0588.d: C0588 is set when the position signal of booster motor A sits below its valid band. GM documents it in its EBCM tables: the 2019 Cadillac XT4 unit trips when a raw sine or cosine value drops under 1,300 counts, or their sum under 3,876, for 10 ms; the 2023 and 2025 tables use a cosine value under 10 counts for 0.15 s, a sine line under 1.047 V or a vector length below 0.25.
s: Check engine lamp together with brake/ABS warning (GM)
Electric assist switched off, high pedal effort
c: Sine or cosine line of the sensor shorted to ground
Missing sensor supply, signals collapse toward zero
Sensor element or target magnet damaged, amplitude too small

C0589.d: C0589 is the high counterpart: a sine or cosine line of motor A's position sensor reads above its permitted maximum. In GM's 2019 XT4 brake module a raw value above 2,795 counts, or a sum above 4,327, for 10 ms sets it; the 2023 and 2025 EBCM tables trip on a cosine reading above 4,075 counts lasting 0.15 s, a sine input above 2.252 V, or a calculated vector length above 1.14.
s: Brake assist warning with check engine lamp (GM)
Hard pedal, assist withdrawn
c: Sensor signal line shorted to the sensor supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground lifting the signals to the upper limit
Internal sensor fault in the booster unit

C058A.d: C058A covers a position signal of booster motor A that is electrically valid but not believable. GM uses it widely: its 2016 and 2019 hybrid tables flag a rotor angle changing faster than 73° per ms, the 2019 IBC unit an invalid Hall pattern (all three high or all low) and a frozen signal, the XT4 module a vector length outside 0.6889–1.2996, and the 2023/2025 tables angle jumps beyond 711.2 rad/s – each Type A with
s: Brake assist failure message, abnormal pedal feel
Check engine and brake warning lamps (GM)
Fault may be hard to read out with a normal scan tool
c: Position sensor delivering implausible angles (Hall element or sine/cosine sensor degraded)
Intermittent contact or interference on the sensor lines causing angle jumps
Booster unit internal fault or position data no longer matching the stored calibration

C058B.d: C058B reports an open circuit at the position sensor of booster motor B. Such a second sensor exists where the booster has a second motor or winding system with its own commutation, or where the rotor angle is measured twice for safety.
s: Brake system warning with service message
Possibly reduced assist or limited assistance functions
c: Broken signal or supply wire of position sensor B
Loose or corroded contact in the sensor B connector
Failed sensor element B inside the booster

C058C.d: C058C applies when the motor B position signal sits below its lower limit – usually a sensor line shorted to ground, a missing sensor supply or a damaged sensor element. No manufacturer publishes this code; GM limits its documented position checks to motor A, where C0588 trips in the XT4 module below 1,300 counts.
s: Brake warning lamp
Assist may continue on one channel with reduced dynamics
c: Signal line of sensor B shorted to ground
Supply of sensor B missing or too low
Sensor element B or its magnet degraded, signal amplitude too small

C058D.d: C058D is set when a signal of motor B's position sensor exceeds its upper limit, for example because a sensor line touches supply voltage or the sensor ground has opened. No manufacturer documents C058D publicly; the range/performance case of the same sensor is C058E, which Stellantis lists for the Jeep Wagoneer eBooster.
s: Brake system warning and message
Assist weaker or switched off depending on design
c: Signal line of sensor B shorted to supply or battery voltage
Open ground of sensor B lifting the signal
Internal fault of sensor B in the booster

C058E.d: C058E concerns a second rotor angle channel of the electric booster motor whose readings are electrically valid but not believable. In GM's 2019 integrated brake control unit this is MPS2, a SENT sensor checked against the faster SPI sensor MPS1 of the same motor: a gap above 2° plus a 3° speed allowance, opposite directions or a changed rest offset for 100 ms set it, Type A with MIL.
s: Service Brake Assist message in the instrument cluster
Hard brake pedal needing more effort, longer stopping distance
Check engine lamp via the brake module request (P25A2)
c: Brake control module calibration causing false correlation faults (GM PIT5638)
Second rotor position sensor in the booster drifting or failing
Fault inside the brake control module or eBooster unit (replaced together)
Poor contact in the booster sensor connector

C058F.d: C058F covers the case where regenerative braking does not deliver the torque the brake system has planned with. In a blended brake the brake module asks the electric drive for generator torque, usually the smaller of the available capacity and the driver's demand, estimates what actually arrives and adds friction braking for the rest, as a GM/BMW/Daimler/Chrysler patent explains.
s: Regenerative braking reduced or disabled, friction brakes do more work
Uneven deceleration or changed pedal feel during light braking
Shorter electric range on plug-in hybrids and EVs
Brake or hybrid system warning message
c: Electric drive or inverter delivering less generator torque than requested
Traction battery unable to absorb charge (full, hot or cold)
Torque arbitration or estimation software in the brake or hybrid module
Missing or delayed torque messages between brake and drive modules

C0590.d: C0590 means the current measured in the drive of booster motor A is too high, mostly checked while the bridge is idle and almost nothing should flow. GM uses it in several units, always Type A with MIL: its 2016/2019 hybrid booster trips on leakage current above 20 A for 5 ms, the XT4 module on an idle offset above 36.1 A or a phase current above 200 A, and the 2023/2025 EBCM tables on a shunt offset above 38 A for 0
s: Brake assist warning, much higher pedal effort
Check engine, ABS or brake warning lamps on
Regenerative braking and automatic brake functions unavailable
c: Leaking or partly conducting MOSFET in the booster motor bridge
Shunt or measuring amplifier offset drifted upward
Winding short in booster motor A drawing excess current
Bridge driver chip failing its overcurrent self-test

C0591.d: C0591 is the low counterpart: the current value of booster motor A lies below what is plausible, in practice a negative reading when the motor is at rest. In GM's 2016/2019 hybrid booster a leakage reading under −20 A counts while a half bridge is idle; the 2023/2025 EBCM tables set it when the offset taken from the internal shunt falls below −38 A for 0.2 s.
s: Loss of electric brake assist, hard pedal
Check engine and brake warning lamps after one drive
Regenerative braking switched off
c: Current sense amplifier or ADC offset drifted below zero
Cracked solder joint or damaged shunt in the power stage
Unexpected reverse current through a faulty bridge transistor

C0592.d: C0592 reports excessive current in the second motor or second winding system, B, of an electric brake booster. No manufacturer publishes it in this sense; the number appears only in GM's keyword list PIP5094 for 2014 and older vehicles, from an earlier numbering.
s: Brake assist warning, possibly weaker or slower assist
Brake or ABS warning lamp on
c: Shorted or leaking transistor in power module B
Insulation fault in winding system B
Measuring offset of the side B current sensing

C0593.d: C0593 is meant for a current value on booster side B that is too low or negative where the controller expects about zero or a commanded positive current. It is not documented by any manufacturer; like C0592 it shows up only in GM's old keyword list PIP5094 with a different meaning.
s: Brake assist warning message
Assist weaker under hard braking if only side A remains
c: Zero point of the side B current measurement drifted
Defective power module B or its driver chip
High resistance in a side B phase connection

C0594.d: C0594 judges whether booster motor A moves as commanded, not its wiring. GM's 2016/2019 hybrid booster flags a motor turning against the commanded direction (under 15 rad/s while more than 25 rad/s is requested), more than seven direction reversals, oscillation with the brake applied, or unintended backward rotation above 40 rad/s.
s: Loss of brake assist with a heavy pedal
Check engine and brake warning lamps on
Booster noise or pedal vibration before the fault sets
c: Binding gear, spindle or plunger inside the booster
Worn or damaged booster motor A
Air or leakage in the hydraulic circuit so pressure does not follow motor travel
Faulty rotor position feedback causing wrong direction or oscillation

C0595.d: C0595 covers the power path inside the booster electronics: master switch, safety relay and the six-transistor bridge driver. GM's 2016/2019 hybrid booster switches its master switch on, off and on again at start-up and expects the voltage ratio behind it above 0.88.
s: Loss of brake assist, longer and softer pedal with more force needed
Service StabiliTrak or brake messages, traction lamp on
Check engine lamp (requested by the brake module)
c: Defective bridge driver chip or its SPI communication
Motor safety relay or master switch not switching correctly
Supply voltage dips or poor module ground

C0596.d: C0596 questions the current measurement of booster motor A itself rather than the motor. GM's 2016/2019 hybrid booster tests its overcurrent comparator at start-up by forcing minimum and maximum PWM and reading the comparator output back over a feedback line, while the voltage behind the master switch must sit near zero or near battery voltage; a hardware overcurrent flag on that line during operation also sets it (3
s: Brake assist warning right after switching on
Heavy brake pedal, check engine lamp on
c: Faulty current sense amplifier or motor driver chip
Overcurrent comparator or its feedback line not responding
Supply voltage outside the test window during start-up

C0597.d: C0597 is a summary code for the first brake system control module: it cannot carry out its function properly, and the failure type byte narrows the cause. Toyota uses C059746 (calibration or parameter memory) on 2020–22 Corolla, Corolla Cross and RAV4 with a parking brake warning, cured by reprogramming the skid control unit (T-SB-0078-21), and C059704 (internal failure) on the 2022–23 Tundra, covered by a software c
s: Service Brake System or parking brake malfunction message
ABS, stability control and possibly check engine lamps on
Changed brake pedal effort
c: Outdated or corrupted brake module software or calibration data
Low battery voltage or poor power and ground connections, especially in cold
Internal fault of the brake control unit or integrated master cylinder

C0598.d: C0598 is the same summary check for a second brake control module, B. Such a module is found where braking is split between two units: Bosch gives its integrated power brake a separate backup unit for automated driving, so the vehicle still stops if the main unit fails.
s: Brake system warning message
Driver assistance or automated driving functions unavailable
Reduced brake assist if the module handles boosting
c: Software or calibration fault in brake module B
Power supply or ground problem of module B
Internal hardware fault of module B
Fault on the link between the two brake modules

C0599.d: C0599 means the control unit of an electric brake booster finds no valid calibration data. Stand-alone electromechanical boosters such as Bosch's iBooster carry their own controller, which converts the reading of a built-in differential travel sensor into motor commands; how the pedal feels is set by software parameters.
s: Brake warning or service brake assist message in the cluster
Hard brake pedal with reduced power assist
Driver assistance functions using the booster (e.g. emergency braking) unavailable
c: Booster or its control module replaced without running the setup/calibration routine
Software update or programming of the booster module aborted or incomplete
Internal memory fault in the booster control module losing stored data

C059A.d: C059A concerns active rear-axle steering: its control module lacks the calibration it needs to position the rear wheels. Systems like ZF's AKC turn the rear wheels by a few degrees with an electrically driven spindle, either through one central actuator or one per wheel.
s: Rear steering warning in the cluster and rear wheel steering inactive
Larger turning circle and changed handling at speed
Steering wheel slightly off centre on straight roads
c: Rear steering module or actuator replaced without centre calibration
Programming or setup after a software update not completed
Suspension or alignment work requiring a new rear steering zero point
Low 12 V supply interrupting the calibration routine

C059B.d: The brake module cannot confirm that pressure sensor B has been calibrated and that its sensitivity is right. GM uses C059B in the brake controller of its 2016 and 2019 hybrid tables for the rear-left wheel pressure sensor: during a test pulse the sensor response must stay between 90 % and 110 %, checked only after at least one completed offset learn, with low master cylinder pressure and no ABS, traction or stabilit
s: ABS and stability control warning lamps on, MIL possible
Regenerative braking blending or ESC functions restricted
c: Pressure sensor responding outside the allowed test-pulse window
Calibration or offset learn not completed after module or hydraulic unit replacement
Brake control module storing or evaluating calibration data incorrectly

C059C.d: For pressure sensor C the module finds no confirmed calibration record. Such a record usually holds the zero offset and a status flag written on the assembly line or by the scan tool.
s: ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Stability control or brake assist functions switched off
c: Sensor calibration not performed after replacing the brake module or modulator
Calibration aborted because the pedal was pressed or the vehicle moved
Stored data does not match the fitted sensor (checksum or ID)

C059D.d: C059D flags missing calibration data for a fourth hydraulic pressure sensor. No manufacturer publishes this code.
s: ABS and ESC warning lamps on
Brake pressure based functions such as hill hold or brake blending limited
c: Calibration of the sensor not done after hydraulic unit or module replacement
Code stored from an earlier event, sensor already calibrated
Brake module losing calibration data in its memory

C059E.d: C059E reports that sensor E, one more pressure sensor in a multi-sensor brake unit, has never been calibrated successfully or that its record is lost. No maker documents C059E publicly; for sensor E only the circuit codes C059F–C05A2 exist.
s: ABS/ESC or brake system warning lamp on
Brake assist or stability functions disabled
c: Calibration run while the vehicle moved or the brake pedal was pressed
Calibration skipped after replacing the brake module or hydraulic unit
Sensor offset too large or unstable so the calibration is rejected

C059F.d: The signal of brake pressure sensor E sits below its valid window. Analogue brake pressure sensors run on 5 V and report roughly 0.5–4.5 V; a Bosch trainer notes such a sensor shows under 1 V with the brake released.
s: ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Stability control and pressure-based brake functions switched off
c: Signal wire of the sensor shorted to ground
Open 5 V supply or signal wire pulled low by the module input
Pressure sensor failed internally (often part of the hydraulic unit)

C05A0.d: C05A0 is set when sensor E reports a voltage above its usable range. In the Denso patent on vehicle pressure sensors the band from 4.7 to 5 V is reserved for faults, and a lost ground wire pushes the output into it through the divider formed by the sensor's internal resistance and the module's pull-down resistor.
s: ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Stability control unavailable, brake lights may be requested falsely on some systems
c: Signal shorted to the 5 V reference or to battery voltage
Open sensor ground lifting the output to the upper rail
Sensor signalling an internal fault at full scale

C05A1.d: This code points to an interrupted circuit of sensor E: a broken signal, 5 V supply or ground wire, or a connector that has lost contact. No maker documents C05A1 publicly.
s: ABS/ESC warning lamp on, possibly coming and going
Stability control and brake assist switched off
c: Corroded or loose connector at the sensor or hydraulic unit
Broken signal, supply or ground wire
Internal open circuit in the sensor

C05A2.d: Here sensor E delivers a voltage that is electrically valid but does not fit the braking situation: a drifting zero point, wrong gain or a value that disagrees with other pressure signals. No maker documents C05A2 publicly.
s: ABS and ESC warning lamps on
Stability or regenerative brake functions reduced
c: Sensor zero point or gain drifted with age or temperature
Residual pressure trapped in the circuit during the zero learn
Ground offset between sensor and module distorting the reading

C05A3.d: Active wheel speed sensors are fed by the ABS module and send their pulses back as a current on the same pair of wires, as HELLA explains. C05A3 reports that this common supply is too high or cannot be switched off.
s: ABS, traction and stability control warning lamps on at the same time
Several or all wheel speed signals lost, speedometer may drop out
MIL on (GM)
c: Wheel speed sensor wire chafed and shorted to battery voltage
Supply switch or ASIC in the brake module stuck on
Water in a wheel speed sensor connector bridging to a powered circuit

C05A4.d: The shared feed for the active wheel speed sensors is too low for them to work. In GM's hybrid tables of 2016 and 2019 the brake controller measures, via an internal comparator, the voltage between the sensor supply line and the signal line and sets C05A4 below 6.7 V for 0.06 s while system voltage is above 6.9 V, Type A with MIL; it also blocks the single-wheel codes such as C0500–C0504.
s: ABS, traction and stability control lamps on, MIL possible
Several wheel speed codes at once, often with low-voltage codes
Hard starting or no start when the 12 V battery is the cause
c: Wheel speed sensor wiring shorted to ground, pulling the shared supply down
Sensor supply stage inside the brake module failing

C05A5.d: Supply B is a second power feed for the pump motor of the brake unit; C05A5 reports it as missing or open. A second feed is found where the motor or its drive is built redundantly.
s: ABS/ESC or brake system warning on
Reduced pressure build-up or loss of redundancy message
c: Blown fuse or fusible link in the B supply
Open wire or loose terminal in the B feed to the brake unit
Internal fault in the second power stage of the brake module

C05A6.d: C05A6 says the second pump motor feed, supply B, carries more voltage than allowed. Overvoltage strains the motor and above all the transistors that switch it; gate driver ICs for brake motors such as TI's DRV8305-Q1 therefore watch their supply and raise an overvoltage warning in the mid-30 V range.
s: ABS/ESC warning lamp on, possibly with other overvoltage codes
Very bright lights or battery warning if charging is the cause
c: Alternator or DC/DC converter regulating too high
Jump start or battery charger with excessive voltage
Voltage measurement fault in the brake module

C05A7.d: Supply B of the pump motor reads below its lower limit. The pump motor draws high current, so a weak 12 V battery, corroded terminals, a fuse holder with high resistance or a poor ground show up first under load.
s: ABS/ESC lamp on, often after cold starts or long standstill
Pump motor running audibly slower during self-test
c: Corroded terminal, fuse holder or ground in the B feed
Charging system not keeping up (alternator or DC/DC converter)

C05A8.d: C05A8 means supply B is present but behaves implausibly: it sags too far once the pump starts, recovers too slowly, or does not match the state the module has commanded. That is different from a hard open (C05A5) or a steady high or low reading (C05A6, C05A7).
s: Intermittent ABS/ESC warning, mostly during pump activity
Message about reduced braking redundancy on brake-by-wire vehicles
c: Excessive voltage drop in the B feed when the pump starts
Relay or semiconductor switch in the B path responding slowly or partly
Aged 12 V battery with high internal resistance

C05A9.d: With two feeds for the pump motor, the module can compare them: both come from the same vehicle supply and should read almost alike. C05A9 is set when the two drift apart beyond the allowed margin, even though each may still lie in its own window.
s: ABS/ESC or brake system warning lamp on
Pump operation or brake redundancy restricted
c: Corroded terminal, fuse or connector in only one of the two feeds
Voltage measurement channel in the brake module drifting
Poor ground affecting only one supply path

C05AA.d: C05AA signals that the ABS return or high-pressure pump motor, or its switching stage, has become too hot. Few units have a sensor on the motor, so the temperature is usually modelled.
s: ABS or stability control temporarily unavailable
ABS or brake warning lamp on, often clearing after cooling down
c: Long ABS, traction or stability interventions, e.g. on rough or slippery roads
Stiff pump or worn motor brushes raising current and heat
Module ambient sensor or temperature model giving false values

C05AB.d: C05AB concerns the separation valve that decouples the driver's master cylinder from the wheel circuits while the brakes work by wire, so that pedal pressure does not cut into regenerative braking. It is usually open without current, so the pedal acts on the wheels if power fails, as in Continental's brake-by-wire layout.
s: Pedal kickback or vibration during braking
Regenerative braking reduced, brake warning message
Brakes switch to direct pedal operation with higher effort
c: Dirt or debris on the valve seat causing leakage
Valve coil or its driver in the module not switching properly
Old or wrong brake fluid making the valve sluggish
Pressure sensor errors making the valve look faulty

C05AC.d: C05AC names one specific failure: the separation valve of the blended brake stays closed when it should open. Toyota's patent for a hybrid brake defines this closure failure and shows how it is pinned down: the control pressure sensor lags its target by more than a set amount for too long, the sensor passes its self-test and the upstream linear valve demonstrably delivers fluid, so the blockage must be the separation
s: Brake warning, assist and regeneration off
Higher pedal effort, longer stopping distance in backup mode
Uneven braking between axles possible
c: Valve armature stuck by contamination or corrosion
Open coil or wiring so a normally closed valve cannot open
Valve driver stage in the brake module defective

C05AD.d: C05AD is the overall check of a blended brake: does the hydraulic pressure built by wire match what the controller asked for? GM's 2016 and 2019 hybrid tables (brake module BSC1) compare actual and target boost-piston pressure, for the by-wire side as well as the master cylinder side: more than 4,000 kPa too high points to a false high sensor value, more than 1,500 kPa too low to a low sensor value, an empty accumula
s: Brake warning and check engine lamps
Soft or inconsistent pedal, braking stronger or weaker than expected
Regenerative braking reduced
c: Brake pressure sensor reading too high or too low
Low accumulator pressure or weak hydraulic pump
Air in the hydraulic circuit after service
External or internal leak in the brake hydraulics

C05AE.d: C05AE means the brake module lacks a valid zero calibration for the measuring channels of its pump motor. In GM's 2016 and 2019 hybrid brake module (BSC1) the motor voltages are read through a sigma-delta modulator that needs a 0 V calibration; with the ignition on, more than 6.9 V system voltage and the pump off, the code sets if the raw generator voltage reading falls outside 14–23.8 or the drop across the pump rel
s: ABS and brake warning lamps plus check engine lamp
ABS or stability functions limited until the calibration succeeds
c: Stored zero calibration missing or invalid after module replacement or programming
Low or unstable supply voltage during the calibration
Pump motor relay or shunt in the module out of tolerance

C05AF.d: C05AF is the plausibility check of the current measurement on booster side B, the second motor or winding system. No manufacturer publishes it.
s: Brake assist or brake system warning
Possibly weaker assist under hard braking
c: Faulty current sense amplifier of side B
Zero offset of side B outside its allowed band
Damaged shunt or solder joint in power module B

C05B0.d: C05B0 reports lost fluid or volume in a hydraulic circuit the maker designates C; at GM its meaning has changed over time. GM's 2016–2019 hybrid brake controllers used it for the front axle circuit: wheel behaviour not matching vehicle deceleration during ABS or EBD for 1 s, or master cylinder pressure above rear axle pressure at constant pedal.
s: Service brake assist or brake system message, brake warning lamp
Longer or softer pedal travel
MIL on (GM)
c: Caliper pistons pushed back during pad work and not reseated before driving (GM 22-NA-247)
Air in the plunger or brake circuit after service or bleeding
Real fluid leak at a line, hose, caliper or valve
Brake module software calibration causing false detection (GM PIT5638)

C05B1.d: C05B1 is the leak code for hydraulic circuit D. The only public maker use is GM's hybrid brake controller of 2016–2019, where it covers the rear axle circuit.
s: Brake and ABS warning lamps on, MIL possible
Longer pedal travel and weaker rear braking
c: Fluid leak at a rear brake line, hose or caliper
Internal leakage of an inlet or outlet valve in the hydraulic unit
Air in the rear circuit after service

C05B2.d: C05B2 flags a mismatch between how far the driver has turned the wheel and how quickly the car actually rotates about its vertical axis. The stability controller turns steering wheel angle and road speed into an expected yaw rate through a single-track vehicle model; a Siemens patent applies that model only up to about 4 m/s² of lateral acceleration.
s: ESC and often traction control warning lamp on
Stability control interventions unavailable
Steering wheel off-centre when driving straight, if alignment is the cause
c: Steering angle sensor not recalibrated after wheel alignment, steering or column work
Yaw rate sensor or sensor cluster loose, rotated or wrongly installed
Offset drift or internal fault in the yaw rate or steering angle sensor
Mismatched tyres or bent steering parts making the vehicle model invalid

C05B3.d: C05B3 means the third temperature channel of an electromechanical brake booster has dropped below its usable band. Mitsubishi documents the code for the Outlander PHEV: the DTC index pairs it with the brake unit's own code C18FC-18, EBA temperature sensor 1, and lights the brake system warning lamp plus the MIL after two trips.
s: Brake system warning lamp on
Check engine lamp on after two trips (Mitsubishi)
Braking assist usually unchanged
c: Fault in the temperature detection inside the electric brake unit's control module
Corroded or loose brake unit connector or damaged harness
Supply disturbance during start-up distorting the reading

C05B4.d: C05B4 is the upper-limit counterpart: temperature channel C of the electric booster reports a value above its permitted maximum. In Mitsubishi's Outlander PHEV index it stands next to C18FC-19, again EBA temperature sensor 1, with the same lamp logic – brake system warning lamp and MIL after the second trip.
s: Brake system warning lamp on
MIL on after the second trip (Mitsubishi)
Code returns immediately after clearing if the unit is defective
c: Temperature circuit on the brake unit's control board defective
Poor contact at the brake unit connector or chafed wiring
Genuinely excessive electronics temperature after heavy booster use

C05B5.d: C05B5 is reserved for an interrupted circuit of booster temperature sensor C. No manufacturer documents it publicly; Mitsubishi, the one maker naming sensor C codes, reports problems with this channel only as C05B3 or C05B4.
s: Brake or brake system warning lamp on
Booster may restrict assist as a precaution, depending on design
c: Cracked thermistor body or broken lead inside the booster
Fractured solder joint on the control board from vibration or heat cycles
Open wire or pin where the sensor is wired externally

C05B6.d: C05B6 targets a sensor C reading that is electrically inside its band yet does not behave like a real temperature: it stays flat during long assist phases, lags far behind the other channels, or contradicts the thermal estimate of the module. No manufacturer publishes this code.
s: Brake system warning lamp on
Assist reduced earlier than usual during long descents or repeated braking
c: Thermistor resistance drifted through ageing, moisture or micro-cracks
Sensor lost thermal contact with the part it should measure
Thermal model or calibration in the booster control unit not matching the hardware

C05B7.d: C05B7 is meant for a temperature C signal that jumps or briefly drops out rather than failing permanently. No manufacturer documents it publicly.
s: Brake system warning lamp flickers or appears only at times
Code returns after clearing, often after rough roads or temperature changes
c: Cracked solder joint or lead at the thermistor
Loose pin or fretting corrosion at the booster connector
Moisture reaching the sensing element through a damaged coating

C05B8.d: The rotor position sensor of booster motor A – Hall, magnetoresistive or a digital SENT angle sensor – is fed from a regulated 5 V output of the brake control unit. C05B8 reports that this feed is interrupted.
s: Brake warning lamp and message such as service brake assist
Noticeably harder brake pedal
Regenerative or electronic brake functions unavailable
c: Broken supply wire or pin between control unit and motor position sensor
Sensor supply output in the brake control unit failed
Internal open in the position sensor's supply path

C05B9.d: C05B9 is set when the feed voltage for motor A's position sensor sags below its lower limit. No manufacturer publishes C05B9; as a reference point, GM's 2019 brake module calls its 5 V sensor supplies low below 4.85 V lasting 100 ms, but books that under C05D1 or C05BB.
s: Brake warning lamp, often with several sensor codes at once
Brake pedal feels hard, assist reduced
c: Supply line chafed through and shorted to ground
Defective position sensor or another sensor on the same rail loading the supply
Weak sensor supply regulator in the control unit

C05BA.d: C05BA covers the opposite case: the 5 V feed of motor A's position sensor rises above its upper limit. The usual culprit is a supply line touching a battery-voltage wire, less often a regulator that has lost control.
s: Brake warning lamp and assist warning message
Hard brake pedal, longer stopping effort
c: Supply line shorted to a battery-voltage circuit in the harness
Sensor supply regulator in the control unit no longer regulating
Poor control unit ground shifting the measured supply voltage

C05BB.d: GM uses C05BB in the integrated brake control of 2019 models. There the processor generates two 5 V sensor supplies; each feeds one pedal travel channel plus one motor position channel.
s: Check engine lamp and brake warning on the first trip (GM)
Service brake assist message, hard pedal
Fault remains until the ignition is switched off
c: Defective motor position sensor loading the shared supply
Defective pedal travel sensor on the same supply
Fault on the brake control unit's circuit board
Intermittent contact in the sensor supply wiring

C05BC.d: C05BC reports an interrupted supply for the position sensor of booster motor B. A B channel exists where the actuator carries a second motor or winding set, or measures its rotor angle twice for redundancy.
s: Brake warning lamp, assist may remain partly available
Reduced maximum assist or slower pressure build-up
c: Broken wire or pushed-back pin in the motor B sensor supply
Second sensor supply output in the control unit failed
Open inside the motor B position sensor

C05BD.d: C05BD means the supply of motor B's position sensor reads below its permitted minimum – a ground short, a sensor pulling excess current or a weak regulator. No manufacturer publishes this code.
s: Brake warning lamp on
Assist fades gradually or is limited at high demand
c: Motor B sensor supply line shorted to ground
Damaged motor B position sensor drawing too much current
Second sensor regulator in the control unit weak

C05BE.d: C05BE is stored when the 5 V feed of motor B's position sensor exceeds its upper limit. No manufacturer documents it publicly.
s: Brake warning lamp and assist warning
Possibly further sensor codes if a shared ground is affected
c: Motor B sensor supply shorted to a battery-voltage wire
Open or high-resistance sensor ground raising the measured voltage
Second sensor supply regulator out of regulation

C05BF.d: C05BF concerns a motor B sensor supply that stays inside its hard limits but behaves implausibly – it fluctuates, disagrees with the independent monitor, or does not match the first supply. No manufacturer documents C05BF publicly.
s: Brake warning lamp appearing at times
Assist occasionally reduced, code returns after clearing
c: Intermittent contact or corrosion in the motor B sensor supply wiring
Unstable sensor supply regulator or failing filter capacitor in the control unit
Fault in the supply monitoring circuit itself

C05C0.d: The control unit has no valid learned rest position for channel A of the brake pedal position sensor, so it cannot turn the raw signal into a reliable pedal travel. No manufacturer documents C05C0 publicly.
s: Brake or ABS warning lamp and message in the cluster
Brake lights or cruise control cancel react late or not at all
Regenerative braking or brake assist functions restricted
c: Learn procedure not run after sensor or module replacement
Learn routine aborted because the pedal was touched or the vehicle moved
Sensor channel A faulty or mounted out of position
Learned values lost in the control module memory

C05C1.d: Set when the second, redundant channel B of the brake pedal position sensor lacks a stored zero point. Many electric and hybrid brake pedals read travel twice so that one channel can cross-check the other; Bosch builds such pedal travel sensors with a magnetic field sensor and two redundant outputs.
s: Brake warning lamp or service message
Reduced redundancy, some assist or regeneration functions disabled
c: Channel B not learned after a repair or software update
Learn conditions not met (pedal pressed, vehicle rolling)
Channel B of the pedal sensor faulty or out of tolerance

C05C2.d: The electric booster or integrated brake unit has found its drive motor A, or the power stage feeding it, too hot. GM uses the code in several EBCM tables, all Type A with MIL: one design trips above 154 °C estimated motor temperature or on a bridge driver over-temperature shutdown, the Cadillac XT4 unit above 120 °C and 142 °C rotor/ECU temperature, 23OBDG07 and 25OBDG03B also when torque limiting stops the plunger
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and brake warning on GM models
Reduced brake assist, pedal feels harder
Regenerative braking temporarily disabled
c: Long downhill braking or repeated hard stops overheating the motor
Hydraulic fault making the motor run longer than normal
Power stage or bridge driver reporting false or real over-temperature
Low supply voltage forcing current limitation

C05C3.d: Points to the power feed of booster motor A: fuse, supply cable, ground or the module input that carries battery current to the motor stage, rather than the motor windings themselves. No manufacturer documents C05C3 publicly.
s: Brake warning lamp, loss or reduction of brake assist
Hard brake pedal, especially at low battery voltage
Further faults for regeneration or driver assistance braking
c: Blown fuse or corroded high-current feed to the booster
Loose or corroded ground of the brake unit
Weak 12 V battery or charging fault causing voltage dips
Internal supply path of the brake module damaged

C05C4.d: The brake controller finds no stored calibration (offset or zero point) for pressure sensor F, the sixth hydraulic pressure sensor in its numbering. Which physical sensor carries the letter F is up to the maker, and none publishes C05C4.
s: ABS, ESC or brake warning lamp on
Stability control or brake assist functions disabled
c: Calibration skipped after module or hydraulic unit replacement
Calibration interrupted by brake application or low voltage
Calibration data lost in the module memory

C05C5.d: Pressure sensor F delivers a voltage inside the electrical window, yet the value does not fit the braking situation: wrong offset at rest, a reading that disagrees with deceleration or the brake switch, or a pressure that does not match pedal travel. No manufacturer documents C05C5 for sensor F.
s: ABS/ESC warning lamp, stability control off
Unusual pedal feel or uneven braking assistance
c: Pressure sensor F drifting or with offset out of tolerance
Calibration not matching after component replacement
Air in the system or hydraulic fault falsifying pressure
Increased contact resistance at the sensor connector

C05C6.d: The signal of pressure sensor F sits below its valid band. Ratiometric 5 V pressure sensors normally output roughly 0.5 to 4.5 V; Denso describes treating 0 to 0.3 V as a fault zone, and with a pull-down resistor at the input a broken supply or signal wire also drags the reading toward zero.
s: ABS, ESC and traction control warning lamps on
Stability and traction control unavailable
c: 5 V reference interrupted or shorted to ground
Internal fault of pressure sensor F

C05C7.d: Here the voltage of pressure sensor F rises above the top of its measuring range. With the common pull-down input, Denso explains that a lost sensor ground lifts the output past 4.7 V, which lies in the upper fault band; a short of the signal to a voltage source has the same effect.
s: ABS/ESC lamp on, stability functions switched off
Live data shows implausibly high brake pressure with pedal released
c: Signal wire shorted to a voltage source
Sensor F reporting an internal fault at the upper rail

C05C8.d: General circuit fault of pressure sensor F, most often a break in one of its three wires (supply, signal, ground) or a connector that has lost contact. Where the reading ends up depends on the input circuit: Honeywell notes that after a power or ground loss the output goes high with a pull-up and low with a pull-down resistor, so an open line can look like C05C6 or C05C7 unless the module tells them apart.
s: ABS and ESC warning lamps on
Stability control and brake assist functions not available
c: Connector unplugged, corroded or with pushed-back pins
Broken wire in the sensor harness
Internal open circuit in sensor F

C05C9.d: Refers to the reference voltage the brake module provides to its hydraulic pressure sensors, not to one sensor's signal. If this feed collapses or rises, every sensor on it reads wrong at once, which is why the module checks the supply separately.
s: Several brake pressure codes at the same time
ABS, ESC and brake assist warnings, functions off
c: Reference line shorted to ground or to battery voltage
One pressure sensor internally shorted, pulling down the shared feed
Sensor supply regulator inside the brake module defective

C05CA.d: Channel A of the travel sensor at the master cylinder input rod reports a signal beyond its upper limit. In GM's booster-type brake modules this channel is a linear position sensor (LiPS) that talks to the EBCM digitally over SENT, so the high error is a message from the sensor itself: the Cadillac XT4 table in 19OBDG03D reacts within 0.033 s on the fast channel, 23OBDG07 and 25OBDG03B after 0.96 s on the slow channe
s: Malfunction indicator lamp plus brake warning on GM models
Reduced brake assist or changed pedal feel
c: Position sensor A reporting out-of-range high internally
Supply voltage of the sensor out of tolerance
Sensor magnet or input rod out of position

C05CB.d: Mirror image of C05CA: channel A of the master cylinder piston travel sensor reports that its value fell below the permitted range. GM documents it for its booster-type EBCMs, where the linear position sensor encodes travel digitally and flags its own low limit violation: the XT4 module acts after 0.033 s on the SENT fast channel, while the 2023 and 2025 tables wait 0.96 s for the slow-channel status, Type A, one tri
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and brake system message
Brake assist reduced, regeneration possibly off
c: Position sensor A reporting out-of-range low

C05CC.d: Channel A (GM calls it PTS1) delivers a travel value that is electrically valid but physically wrong. GM's integrated controller with pedal simulator, the vacuum-free design ZF supplies, checks three things: travel above 38 mm (normal input piston travel is about 25 mm, about 36 mm without boost), a change faster than 700 mm/s, and a learned offset beyond 2.5 mm, each 100 ms, Type A.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and brake warning
Changed pedal feel or reduced assist
Brake lights may react inconsistently
c: Sensor A offset drifted beyond the learn limit
Damaged travel sensor rod or mounting
Pedal not fully returning (floor mat, return spring)

C05CD.d: Channel B of the master cylinder piston travel sensor is stuck at a permanent high level. In GM's booster-type EBCMs the second channel is not sent over SENT like channel A but as a PWM signal around 1 kHz, which is why high and low here mean a line that no longer toggles: the module sets C05CD when it sees a steady high state for 0.2 s, read as a short of the PWM line to supply (19OBDG03D XT4 section, 23OBDG07, 25OB
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and brake warning on GM models
Booster runs on channel A only or reduces assist
c: PWM signal line shorted to supply voltage
Output stage of sensor channel B failed high
Moisture or corrosion bridging pins in the connector

C05CE.d: Here the second, PWM-coded output (channel B) of the piston travel sensor stays permanently low. GM's XT4 brake module and the later 23OBDG07 and 25OBDG03B tables interpret a constant low level for 0.2 s as the signal line shorted to ground, Type A, one trip, MIL.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, brake system warning
Possibly reduced assist or regeneration off
c: PWM signal line shorted to ground
Sensor channel B without supply or ground
Output stage of channel B failed low

C05CF.d: Plausibility fault on channel B (GM: PTS2) while its signal is electrically in range. GM's integrated controller with pedal simulator runs the same checks on B as on A: more than 38 mm of travel, a step faster than 700 mm/s that disagrees with channel A and the simulator pressure model, or an offset beyond 2.5 mm, all with 100 ms and Type A.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and brake warning
Pedal feels different, assist may be reduced
c: Offset of sensor B outside the allowed range
Loose contact causing implausible jumps on channel B
Sensor rod or mounting worn or bent

C05D0.d: Both travel channels are individually plausible, but they disagree with each other. GM's integrated controller votes two out of three: PTS1, PTS2 and a third travel estimate (BAS); if PTS1 and PTS2 differ by more than 2 mm and one of them also deviates from the third value by over 2 mm, that channel is declared failed after 100 ms.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and brake warning
Brake system switches to reduced mode, regeneration may be off
c: One sensor channel drifting away from the other
Mechanical play at the sensor or input rod
Contact resistance on one channel only

C05D1.d: Fault on the reference supply of the master cylinder piston (pedal travel) sensor. GM's integrated brake controller provides two 5 V supplies, each feeding one pedal travel channel and one motor position channel; C05D1 covers the first (PTS1/MPS1), C05BB the second.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, brake warning and loss of assist
Further codes for pedal travel and motor position sensors
c: Supply line shorted to ground or to another voltage
Pedal travel or motor position sensor loading the supply
Supply circuit on the control module board defective

C05D2.d: The piston has travelled further than the measured pressure justifies, a sign that fluid escapes or a sensor misreads. GM's integrated controller models the simulator pressure from pedal travel and sets C05D2 when the model exceeds the measured value by more than 20 bar (250 ms in 19OBDG03D, 500 ms in 25OBDG04B), naming master cylinder or simulator seal leakage and an in-range pressure sensor fault.
s: Longer, softer brake pedal with higher pedal force
Loss of brake assist and messages in the driver information centre
Malfunction indicator lamp on GM models
c: Internal leakage at master cylinder or simulator seals
Simulator pressure sensor reading too low within range
Air in the hydraulic system after service

C05D3.d: The pressure the driver generates is higher than the measured pedal travel would predict, a hard pedal pattern. GM's integrated controller sets C05D3 when the measured simulator pressure is more than 20 bar above its travel-based model, outside fast applications, naming a closed or blocked simulator valve, a seized simulator and an in-range sensor fault.
s: Check engine lamp on together with brake system message
Brake pedal feels spongy, hard or unusual
c: Weak or discharged 12 V battery (GM PIT6012)
Pedal simulator valve closed or blocked
Pressure or travel sensor misreading within range

C05D4.d: No valid zero calibration exists for the master cylinder piston travel sensors. GM's integrated controller stores the end-of-line zeroing of its pedal travel sensors in non-volatile memory and reloads it each drive; C05D4 sets within 10 ms after start if the stored status shows the learn failed.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and brake warning after start
Brake system in reduced mode until calibrated
c: Zeroing not done after replacement of the brake unit
Calibration disturbed by vehicle movement or pedal input
Sensor offset too large, too small or unsteady
Memory error in the brake control module

C05D5.d: Electrical fault of the solenoid valve that separates the master cylinder from the wheel circuits in by-wire operation, so pressure comes from the motor and the pedal works against a simulator. In GM's booster-type EBCMs (XT4, 23OBDG07, 25OBDG03B) the valve driver reports over-current of about 4 to 6.5 A, an output stage above 195-220 °C, a lost power ground or lost freewheeling within 0.03 s.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and brake warning
Loss of brake assist, pedal works on the master cylinder directly
ESC and traction control limited
c: Valve coil shorted or open inside the hydraulic unit
Valve driver stage or ASIC in the module defective
Poor power ground of the brake module
Valve overheated by excessive activation time

C05D6.d: The electric power steering controller has found that its own processor, or the cross-check between its processors, is not working as expected. Toyota documents the code as C05D604 in the ECU of the EPS steering gear: 2019–2020 RAV4 and RAV4 Hybrid light the EPS warning in red or yellow at start-up or while driving (T-SB-0061-20), and the 2022 Tundra and Lexus LX 600 log it at start-up, often together with C15D704.
s: Red or yellow power steering warning lamp
Steering suddenly heavier or assist reduced
Fault appears mainly right after starting the vehicle
c: EPS controller software flags a false processor fault, update available
Supply voltage dip during engine start disturbs the self-test
Internal hardware fault in the steering control module

C05D7.d: Covers the output that drives the brake transmission shift interlock, the solenoid that keeps the selector in park until the brake pedal is pressed. In the US, FMVSS 114 has required this lock since 1 September 2010 on vehicles up to 4,536 kg fitted with an automatic gearbox and a park position.
s: Selector cannot be moved out of park despite pressing the brake
Selector leaves park without the brake applied
No clicking of the interlock when the brake is pressed
c: Interlock solenoid coil open or shorted
Damaged wiring or corroded connector at the shifter
Driver stage in the shifter or body module faulty
Brake light switch signal missing, so the lock is never released

C05D8.d: The AWD controller sees no plausible current path in the output that drives the actuator of clutch A, typically an open coil, motor winding or wire. Depending on the design, the actuator is an electromagnetic coil (JTEKT ITCC: coil current sets the transmitted torque) or an electric motor that turns a ball ramp through a worm gear, as in a Magna disconnect coupling.
s: AWD warning lamp or message, vehicle drives on one axle only
Wheel spin on slippery surfaces when pulling away
c: Actuator coil or motor winding open
Rear drive unit motor with misaligned magnet ring (Ford Bronco Sport 2.0L)
Broken wire or loose connector at the rear axle
Output stage in the AWD control module faulty

C05D9.d: The actuator circuit of clutch A is electrically intact, but the actuator does not respond as commanded, for example the measured current, motor speed or achieved torque differs from the target. Ford uses this code widely in its AWD module.
s: AWD fault message, AWD inoperative for the rest of the trip
Powertrain malfunction (wrench) lamp on
Function returns after restarting the vehicle
c: Low battery state of charge or weak supply voltage
Actuator motor worn or misassembled (magnet ring)
Ball ramp or gear train of the actuator binding

C05DA.d: The voltage measured on the clutch A actuator line stays below the expected level, which usually means a short to ground somewhere between the control module and the coil or motor. Mitsubishi Electric describes a method for an electromagnetic driveline clutch: a high-side PWM transistor and a low-side switch feed the coil, the terminal voltages are compared with their normal values, and on a ground fault both transis
s: AWD switched off with warning lamp
Fault returns immediately after clearing
c: Actuator wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Water or corrosion in the connector at the axle
Coil or motor winding shorted to the housing

C05DB.d: Set when the clutch A actuator line reads too high, typically because it touches battery voltage or because the low-side switch cannot pull it down. For an electromagnetic clutch, Mitsubishi Electric checks for this short with the selector in P or N by comparing the terminal voltages against normal values, then releases the clutch by turning off both drivers.
s: AWD warning, all-wheel drive disabled
Possible binding or tyre scrub in tight turns if the clutch drags
c: Actuator wire shorted to a supply line in the harness
Output transistor in the AWD module stuck on
Corrosion bridging pins in the actuator connector

C05DC.d: The calculated or measured temperature of clutch A has passed the protection limit, usually after long slipping in sand, snow or while towing. Audi stores C05DC00 in the AWD control unit of quattro ultra models: in TSB 2075681/1 the technician drives circles at full lock below 10 km/h for up to 15 minutes until the yellow four-wheel drive overheating lamp comes on, then erases the entry.
s: Yellow AWD overheating warning
Less drive to the secondary axle until the clutch has cooled
Engine power briefly reduced during wheel spin
c: Long periods of wheel slip in deep snow, sand or mud
Towing or steep climbs with heavy load
Different tyre sizes or wear front to rear force constant slip

C05DD.d: The AWD controller has commanded clutch A to close, but the speed difference across it or the actuator feedback shows that it is not transmitting the expected torque or has stayed open. Typical reasons are worn plates, a sticking actuator or a ball ramp that cannot travel far enough.
s: AWD malfunction message, vehicle behaves like two-wheel drive
Wheel spin and traction control interventions on slippery roads
c: Clutch plates worn, slipping under load
Actuator or ball ramp sticking short of full travel
Wrong, aged or low clutch fluid
Damaged shift fork or dog teeth in the decoupling unit

C05DE.d: Clutch A keeps transmitting torque or stays connected although the controller has ordered it to open. Front and rear axles are then forced to turn together, which shows up as binding, tyre scrub or droning in tight, slow turns.
s: Binding, hopping or tyre scrub when parking or in tight turns
Droning or vibration from the rear axle
AWD malfunction message
c: Clutch plates welded or swollen after overheating
Actuator or ball ramp seized in the applied position
Aged clutch fluid causing drag and stick-slip
Worn shift fork keeps a dog clutch engaged

C05DF.d: The engagement sequence of clutch A did not finish correctly: the actuator ran, but synchronisation, connection feedback or the timing check failed. This matters most for disconnecting systems that must reconnect a stationary driveline on the move.
s: AWD unavailable message, sometimes only for one trip
Clunk from the driveline when AWD tries to engage
c: Speeds not matched in time before the clutch closes
Actuator too slow because of low voltage or wear
Engagement feedback sensor reports wrong state

C05E0.d: General electrical fault in the sensor that reports where the clutch A actuator stands, without the controller narrowing it down to low, high or intermittent. Electromechanical AWD clutches need this signal because the motor angle maps to plate travel and clamping force.
s: AWD warning, all-wheel drive switched off
Traction loss when pulling away on low grip
c: Position sensor in the actuator faulty
Sensor supply or ground from the AWD module missing

C05E1.d: The clutch A position signal is electrically within limits but does not fit what the actuator should be doing, for instance it barely changes while the motor runs or jumps further than the gearing allows. Bosch's transfer-case clutch provides the data for such a cross-check: worm wheel position, motor speed and motor current are all measured, so a position that drifts away from the counted motor rotation stands out.
s: AWD warning, torque transfer to the secondary axle stopped
Fault often sets only after some driving
c: Sensor magnet or target loose or misaligned

C05E2.d: The position signal from the clutch A actuator has dropped below its valid band. On a sensor powered by a reference supply this normally means the signal line is shorted to ground, the supply is missing, or the sensor output is dead.
s: AWD warning lamp on
Vehicle drives with one axle only

C05E3.d: Here the clutch A position signal sits above the highest value a working sensor can deliver. Usual explanations are a signal line touching the supply or battery voltage, a lost sensor ground that lets the output float up, or an internal sensor fault.
s: AWD warning lamp on
All-wheel drive disabled until the fault is repaired
c: Signal wire shorted to supply or battery voltage

C05E4.d: The clutch A position signal drops out or jumps for short moments and then recovers, so the controller sees implausible steps between consecutive samples. The pattern points to a loose pin, a chafed wire that touches only on bumps, or moisture in the connector near the axle, rather than a dead sensor.
s: AWD warning that comes and goes
Short losses of drive to the secondary axle
c: Loose or corroded pin in the sensor connector
Harness chafing at the axle or subframe

C05E5.d: The controller has no valid stored reference for clutch A, typically the touch or kiss point where the plates begin to carry torque. Bosch finds this point on a transfer-case clutch by running the motor at constant speed and intersecting two regression lines from the free-travel and loaded ranges; the run is repeated at engine start or at standstill because wear shifts the curve.
s: AWD warning directly after a repair
All-wheel drive disabled or harsh engagement
c: Learn not run after replacing actuator, clutch or module
Learn routine aborted, for example by low voltage or vehicle movement
Stored values lost after battery disconnection or module fault

C05E6.d: The closed-loop control that drives clutch A to a target position cannot hold or reach it: the deviation between commanded and measured position stays too large for too long. Magna describes an ECU that controls the angular position of the ball ramp actuator ring; Bosch drives its transfer-case clutch motor with a cascaded current and speed controller through an H-bridge; GKN's actuator controller handles fast clutch
s: AWD malfunction message, AWD disabled
Uneven or delayed torque transfer before the fault sets
c: Actuator gear train or ball ramp binding
Weak actuator motor or low supply voltage

C05E7.d: The AWD module finds no usable current path in its driver output for the clutch B actuator, most often an open coil, motor winding, connector or wire. A second clutch exists either in a twin-clutch rear drive unit with one clutch per rear wheel, or as a disconnect stage in the rear axle.
s: AWD warning lamp or message, rear axle no longer driven
Rear locking or torque vectoring function unavailable on twin-clutch units
Fault is present again immediately after clearing
c: Open coil or motor winding in the clutch B actuator
Misaligned magnet ring in the rear drive unit motor (Ford Bronco Sport 2.0L)
Broken wire or corroded connector between AWD module and rear drive unit
Faulty driver stage in the AWD module

C05E8.d: The clutch B actuator circuit is electrically intact, yet its response does not match the command: current, motor movement or the torque built up stays outside the expected band. Ford stores C05E8:71 in the AWD module of 2021–2022 Bronco Sport 2.0L vehicles (SSM 51117), together with C05D9:71 for clutch A; both lead back to the misaligned magnet ring of the rear drive unit motor, and the repair is a new motor instead
s: AWD fault message, all-wheel drive off for the rest of the trip
Reduced traction off-road because one rear wheel is no longer controlled
c: Misaligned magnet ring in the rear drive unit motor (Ford Bronco Sport 2.0L)
Worn or sluggish actuator motor or hydraulic control for clutch B
Low battery voltage limiting actuator current
Binding in the actuator mechanism or clutch pack

C05E9.d: The voltage on the clutch B actuator line reads below the expected value, which points to a short to ground between AWD module and coil or motor, or to a driver stage that pulls the line down. A Mitsubishi Electric clutch patent shows how such a fault is caught: high-side and low-side transistors feed the coil, with the selector in P or N the module checks both terminal voltages against what they should read, and a d
s: AWD warning, all-wheel drive disabled
Fault returns at once after clearing, often after driving through water
c: Chafed actuator wire shorting to ground near the rear axle
Water or corrosion in the rear drive unit connector
Internal short in the clutch B coil or motor

C05EA.d: The clutch B actuator line reads too high, usually from contact with a battery feed or because the low-side switch no longer pulls it down. With coil-type clutches the danger is current flowing although the module wants the clutch open: in JTEKT's ITCC the coil current sets the transmitted torque, so a partly energised coil lets the clutch drag.
s: AWD warning, all-wheel drive disabled
Possible binding or tyre scrub when manoeuvring
c: Actuator wire shorted to a supply line
Low-side switch in the AWD module defective
Corrosion bridging pins in the actuator connector

C05EB.d: The AWD module has calculated or measured that clutch B has passed its permitted temperature, usually after long slipping in deep snow, sand or mud, or when towing. In a twin-clutch rear module the two wheel clutches heat up separately, so one side can reach its limit while the other is still cool, for instance when only one rear wheel spins.
s: AWD overheating or temporarily disabled message
Less drive to the rear until the clutch has cooled
Engine power briefly reduced during wheel spin
c: Long wheel spin on one rear wheel in snow, sand or mud
Towing or climbing with high, continuous torque transfer
Different tyre sizes or wear front to rear causing permanent slip
Aged or wrong fluid in the rear drive unit

C05EC.d: Clutch B was commanded to connect, but speed signals or actuator feedback show that it carries no torque or has stayed open. In disconnecting systems the second clutch is often a positive shift element rather than a friction pack: Audi's quattro ultra releases both a gearbox-side multi-plate clutch and a decoupler in the rear differential, which autozine describes as an electromechanically operated dog clutch on the
s: AWD malfunction message, vehicle drives on the front axle only
Wheel spin and traction control interventions on slippery roads
c: Clutch B actuator sticking or too weak to shift the sleeve
Worn shift fork or damaged dog teeth in the rear differential
Worn friction plates on twin-clutch units
Low or wrong fluid in the rear drive unit

C05ED.d: Clutch B is still connected although the AWD module has ordered it to open. It is the one code of the clutch B group that a manufacturer documents in detail.
s: Sporadic four-wheel drive malfunction message
Rear driveline keeps turning when it should be decoupled, possible noise
c: Worn shift fork in the rear differential (Audi quattro ultra)
Clutch B actuator seized in the engaged position
Welded or swollen plates on friction-type clutch B

C05EE.d: The connection sequence of clutch B did not complete: the actuator moved, but speed matching, position feedback or the time window failed. This concerns above all positive dog clutches, which may only close once both halves turn at almost the same speed.
s: AWD unavailable message, sometimes only for one trip
Clunk or rattle from the rear when AWD tries to connect
c: Speed of the disconnected driveline not matched in time
Slow actuator, often from low voltage or cold, thick fluid
Faulty position or shaft speed feedback
Worn or chipped dog teeth blocking engagement

C05EF.d: The position loop that moves clutch B to a target cannot reach or hold it: commanded and measured actuator position stay apart for too long. Such loops depend on a learned reference.
s: AWD malfunction message, AWD disabled
Delayed or uneven torque transfer before the fault sets
c: Binding ball ramp, gear or shift mechanism
Weak actuator motor or low supply voltage
Learned reference no longer valid after wear or part replacement

C05F0.d: The signal of the rear drive shaft speed sensor stays below its valid range, typically due to an open circuit, a short to ground or a missing sensor supply. The AWD module needs this speed to match a disconnected rear driveline to the wheels before a clutch closes; American Axle's patent feeds a pinion shaft speed sensor into exactly that synchronisation check.
s: AWD warning, all-wheel drive not connected
Vehicle drives in front-wheel drive only
c: Open sensor wire or loose connector
Signal or supply line shorted to ground

C05F1.d: Here the rear drive shaft speed signal reads above its valid range, as caused by a short to supply voltage, a damaged sensor IC or a fault at the module input. With a two-wire Hall sensor the module watches the current between a low and a high level (Allegro A19420: about 7 and 14 mA); a current clearly above the upper band cannot be a speed pulse.
s: AWD warning, all-wheel drive not connected
Fault sets immediately at ignition on
c: Sensor signal line shorted to supply voltage
Damaged sensor IC drawing excessive current
Faulty sensor input in the AWD module

C05F2.d: The speed signal from the rear drive shaft drops out or jumps for short moments and then recovers, so the AWD controller sees pulse gaps or sudden speed steps that no real shaft could make. Such sensors are often two-wire Hall ICs whose supply current toggles between two levels; Allegro specifies about 7 and 14 mA for its A19420 and stresses stable output despite sudden air gap changes, so short dropouts usually poin
s: AWD or 4WD warning appears now and then and disappears again
All-wheel drive briefly unavailable, often on rough roads
Code stored as history without a current fault
c: Loose, corroded or water-affected connector at the sensor
Harness chafed or broken where it flexes near the axle or drive shaft
Sensor not seated firmly, air gap varies with vibration
Damaged or dirty target ring on the shaft

C05F3.d: Catch-all electrical fault for the rear drive shaft speed sensor circuit, stored when the controller detects a problem but does not narrow it to low, high or intermittent. Typical are an open supply or signal wire, a failed sensor IC or a fault in the module input.
s: AWD or 4WD service message, all-wheel drive switched off
Vehicle drives on the primary axle only
No drive shaft speed shown in live data
c: Open signal or supply wire between sensor and module
Connector not latched or pins pushed back
Faulty input stage in the AWD control module

C05F4.d: The rear drive shaft speed is electrically valid but does not fit the rest of the driveline. The controller can compare it with wheel speeds, the axle ratio and the clutch state: with AWD engaged the shaft must follow the rear wheels, and a reading that stays near zero, lags or runs too fast is implausible.
s: AWD warning and all-wheel drive disabled
Rear axle no longer connects in a disconnecting AWD system
Live data shows shaft speed that does not match wheel speeds
c: Air gap too large, sensor not fully seated or wrong spacer
Target ring damaged, loose or covered with metal debris
Wrong sensor, target ring or axle ratio after repair
Slipping AWD clutch makes shaft speed deviate

C05F5.d: The range actuator is the electric gear motor that moves the transfer case between high range, neutral and low range. With this code the controller finds no usable current path in the motor drive circuit, usually an open winding, wire or connector.
s: 4WD service message, low range cannot be selected
Range indicator flashes or does not change
Transfer case stays in its last position
c: Shift motor connector not fully seated or corroded
Broken wire between control module and motor
Open motor winding or worn brushes in the range actuator
Failed output stage in the control module

C05F6.d: The drive circuit of the range actuator is electrically present, but the response does not match the command: motor current, run time or achieved travel fall outside the window the controller expects. Magna describes a range shift motor driven by pulse width modulation in phases, fast to neutral, slower through synchronisation at about 55 to 80 percent of travel, and under PID position control from about 90 percent.
s: Range shifts slow or incomplete
Intermittent 4WD service message, often when cold or at start-up
Shift attempt aborted, transfer case returns to previous range
c: High resistance in ground or supply of the motor circuit
Weak battery or low system voltage during the shift
Worn shift motor drawing abnormal current
Degraded driver stage in the control module

C05F7.d: A range actuator drive line sits below its expected voltage, typically because a motor lead is shorted to ground or the driver pulls it down when it should not. In a reversing gear motor each terminal is alternately the high and the low side, so a ground short on either lead shows up depending on shift direction.
s: 4WD service message, range change refused
Fault may appear only when shifting in one direction
Blown fuse for the transfer case motor possible
c: Motor lead chafed through and shorted to the body or transfer case
Water or corrosion in the shift motor connector
Internal short in the shift motor
Faulty low-side driver in the control module

C05F8.d: A range actuator drive line carries more voltage than the controller expects, for example from a short to battery voltage or because a low-side switch no longer pulls the line down. The risk is a motor that runs or is braked when it should be idle, or a driver that cannot complete a commanded direction.
s: 4WD service message, range shift disabled
Shift motor may hum or run unexpectedly
Transfer case remains in the last selected range
c: Motor lead shorted to a battery-fed wire
Low-side switch in the control module failed open
Corrosion bridging pins in the shift motor connector

C05F9.d: The controller has measured or estimated that the range actuator motor is too hot and blocks further shifts until it cools. Most designs model temperature from motor activity; a Denso patent for a similar shift actuator adds a fixed increment per motor start, lets the estimate decay over time and limits the motor above a protection value of 137 degrees C in its example.
s: Message that 4WD is overheated or temporarily unavailable
Range shifts refused until the system cools
Wrench or 4WD service lamp on
c: Many range shifts in a short time, motor protection active
Low battery charge prolongs motor run time and current
Stiff shift mechanism or blocked shift loads the motor
Worn shift motor drawing excess current

C05FA.d: The range actuator received a valid command and its circuit looks fine, yet the transfer case did not reach the requested range in time or stays in one position. Range shifts use toothed sleeves that can meet tooth on tooth; BorgWarner places a torsion spring between motor and barrel cam so the motor can keep turning and the stored energy finishes the shift once the teeth align.
s: Low range does not engage or does not release
Range indicator keeps flashing
Grinding or clicking from the transfer case during the shift
c: Shift blocked tooth on tooth, often when not rolling or not in neutral
Binding range fork, cam or shift rail inside the transfer case
Worn or seized shift motor gear train
Low or wrong transfer case fluid

C05FB.d: General electrical fault in the circuit of the sensor that reports where the range actuator stands, without narrowing it to low, high or implausible. Designs vary: Magna mounts a programmable linear Hall IC on the transfer case housing that reads a stepped sector plate or the range fork and outputs a duty cycle; BorgWarner uses a single sensor whose probe rides five plateaus on the cam; GM full-size trucks combine ro
s: 4WD service message, range shifts disabled
Range indicator blank or flashing
Further transfer case codes stored at the same time
c: Sensor or actuator connector not fully latched
Open supply, ground or signal wire of the position sensor
Failed position sensor, often integrated in the shift motor

C05FC.d: The range actuator position signal is electrically valid but does not agree with what the actuator is doing: it does not change while the motor runs, lands between defined positions or contradicts a second position input. Magna's sensor resolves its four sector positions to about plus or minus 1.5 degrees, and BorgWarner's target has five plateaus, so a reading between steps is suspicious.
s: Flashing 4WD indicator, range display does not match actual range
Range shifts refused or repeated
4WD service message
c: Sensor target or magnet shifted, loose or worn
Moisture in the actuator, for example via a faulty breather
Sensor drifting with temperature or age
Actuator or module replaced without matching calibration

C05FD.d: The range actuator position signal sits below the lowest value an intact sensor can deliver. With a sensor powered from a reference supply this usually means the signal line is shorted to ground, the supply is missing or the sensor output has failed low.
s: 4WD service message, range shifts disabled
Range indicator shows no valid position

C05FE.d: The range actuator position signal lies above the highest value a working sensor produces. Usual explanations are a signal line touching supply voltage, a lost sensor ground that lets the output float up, or an internal sensor fault.
s: 4WD service message, range shifts disabled
Range display flashes or shows a wrong range
c: Signal wire shorted to supply or battery voltage

C05FF.d: The controller lacks valid reference positions for the range actuator, so it cannot translate sensor readings into high, neutral and low. GM full-size trucks run such a relearn at every start-up: per PIP5089A the transfer case module drives the encoder motor to locate its position, and if a sensor, motor or circuit problem prevents this it sets C0569 and runs no further checks.
s: 4WD service message right after a repair
Range shifts unavailable until the learn has run
Range indicator flashes at start-up
c: Actuator or control module replaced without running the learn routine
Learn routine aborted by a sensor, motor or wiring fault
Stored values lost after battery disconnection or low voltage
